### Describe the misformalization
I may be incorrect, but I believe that there is an error in the statement of ABC. The link is here: https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/ABC.lean

The statement checks that a, b, and c are pairwise coprime using 
`({a, b, c} : Set ℕ).Pairwise Nat.Coprime`
However, looking at the documentation, Pairwise gets rid of identical elements. So it would seem to say that {4, 4, 3} is a set of pairwise coprime integers.


### Trivial proof/disproof
If a = b \neq 1, then {a, b, c} would appear to be pairwise coprime, even though they are not. 

### Suggested fix
There could be a check that a \neq b, for example. 

Discovered in collaboration with Florian Meister.

### Choose either option
- [ ] I plan on working on this issue
- [x] This issue is up for grabs: I would like to see this misformalization fixed by somebody else
title: ABC Conjecture & Pairwise Coprime

> **Affected File:** [`FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/897.lean`](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/897.lean#L98-L124)  
> **Affected Declarations:** `Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.parts.i` (line 103), `Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.parts.ii` (line 121)  
> **Severity:** High — Vacuously eliminates the entire strongly-additive branch of both open conjectures.  
> **Discovery Method:** Idris 2 (`%default total`) dependent-type reformulation audit (flagged missing `GT k 0` obligation).

---

## Current Code

Lines 98–124 of [`FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/897.lean`](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/897.lean#L98-L124):

```lean
@[category research open, question, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_897.variants.parts.i : ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    (∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p) ∨ (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => ((f (n+1) - f n) / (n : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

@[category research open, question, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_897.variants.parts.ii : ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    ((Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) : ℕ × ℕ | p.Prime}).limsup
      (fun (p, k) => (f (p^k) / (p^k : ℝ).log : EReal)) = ⊤) →
    (∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p) ∨ (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) →
    Filter.atTop.limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (f (n+1) / f n : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry
```

---

## Proof of Defect

In both theorems, the left disjunct of the extra hypothesis is intended to state that $f$ is **strongly additive** ($f(p^k) = f(p)$ for all primes $p$ and all **positive** integers $k \ge 1$). However, `k : ℕ` is unconstrained and includes **`k = 0`**:

1. From additivity (`hadd : ∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b`) applied to `a = 1, b = 1`:
   $$f(1) = f(1 \cdot 1) = f(1) + f(1) \implies f(1) = 0.$$
2. From the strongly-additive hypothesis `hstrong : ∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p ^ k) = f p` instantiated at **`k = 0`**:
   $$\forall p,\ p.\text{Prime} \implies f(p) = f(p^0) = f(1) = 0.$$
3. Applying `hstrong` again for arbitrary `k : ℕ`:
   $$\forall k\ p,\ p.\text{Prime} \implies f(p^k) = f(p) = 0.$$
4. Consequently, `(fun (p, k) => (f (p ^ k) / (p ^ k : ℝ).log : EReal))` is identically `0` on `{(p, k) | p.Prime}`, so its `limsup` is `0 ≠ ⊤`, contradicting the growth hypothesis `hlim = ⊤`.

Therefore, **no function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ can simultaneously satisfy `hadd`, `hlim`, and `hstrong`**. The strongly-additive branch of both `erdos_897.variants.parts.i` and `erdos_897.variants.parts.ii` is **vacuously true** (leaving only the completely-additive branch `f (p^k) = k * f p`, which happens to survive `k = 0` because `0 * f p = 0 = f 1`).

---

## Proposed Fix

Restrict `k` to `k ≥ 1` (`k > 0`) in the strongly-additive disjunct on lines 103 and 121:

```lean
-    (∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p) ∨ (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) →
+    (∀ k > 0, ∀ p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p) ∨ (∀ (k p : ℕ), p.Prime → f (p^k) = k*f p) →
```
title: Strongly-Additive Branch of erdos_897.variants.parts.{i,ii} Is Vacuously True Due to Missing k > 0 Guard (FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/897.lean)

body:
### Describe the misformalization / issue with the statement

**OEIS A238281 — counterexamples to `OeisA238281.conjecture_2` at n = 14 and n = 286**

Source: https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/FormalConjectures/OEIS/238281.lean  
OEIS: https://oeis.org/A238281

The strengthened assertion says that for each natural number `n > 1`, `n != 8`, there is a `k` with `0 < k < n` such that `2*k + 1` is prime and the adjacent intervals `((k-1)*n, k*n]` and `(k*n, (k+1)*n]` have equal prime counts.

**Neither n = 14 nor n = 286 has any such k.** This appears to falsify the underlying strengthened conjecture, **not** to demonstrate an incorrect translation into Lean. I am using the available issue template to report the counterexamples.

### Trivial proof/disproof (finite counterexamples)

For `n = 14`, these are all eligible `k` (`2*k+1` prime). The two columns give exact counts of primes in the adjacent intervals:

| k | Left | Right |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 6 | 3 |
| 2 | 3 | 4 |
| 3 | 4 | 3 |
| 5 | 3 | 4 |
| 6 | 4 | 2 |
| 8 | 4 | 1 |
| 9 | 1 | 4 |
| 11 | 2 | 3 |

None has equal counts. For `n = 286`, an exhaustive check of all **104 eligible k** likewise finds no equality; the full candidate table is in `prime_count_verification.csv`.

Checks performed:
- Direct trial-division primality testing and prime counting for the individual counterexamples.
- Sieve-based counting for `2 <= n <= 6000` using the supplied Python script. In this finite range the half-open Lean statement (already excluding `n = 8`) has only the additional exceptions `n = 14, 286`.
- The OEIS wording with **open** intervals also has the previously discussed endpoint exception `n = 2`. The Lean source accounts for this boundary issue.

No Lean-kernel-checked disproof is included. The finite counterexamples do not disprove `conjecture_1`, nor does searching through 6000 prove a corrected statement for all larger n.

### Suggested handling

Please flag `conjecture_2` as **false as currently stated**, if the counterexamples are confirmed. Excluding `14` and `286` as well as `8` would produce a **candidate revision**, not a proven theorem: other exceptions for larger n are not ruled out. The corresponding OEIS comment may also need review.

### Additional context / reproduction

These counterexamples were identified during my independent research using ATLAS, my experimental AI-assisted problem-solving and verification approach.

With ATLAS, I investigate complex mathematical and technical problems by reducing them to their decisive conditions, systematically searching for counterexamples, and verifying the results through reproducible computations.

AI assistance was used in developing the verification scripts. The reported counterexamples were checked using two different computational approaches. No Lean kernel-checked proof is claimed.

The files supplied alongside this report are:

- `beleg_A238281.py`: original Python verification script; requires Python 3 and NumPy. Run: `python3 -I beleg_A238281.py 6000`.
- `ausgabe.txt`: original recorded output.
- `prime_count_verification.csv`: independently regenerated exact candidate-count table for n = 14 and n = 286 (open intervals; these agree with half-open intervals for these two n because their positive multiples at the interval boundaries are composite).
- `BELEG_A238281.md`: original German report.

The counterexamples were found during **ATLAS**, my experimental AI-assisted investigation project. AI assistance was used to develop the checks. The data have been cross-checked computationally, but this is not a Lean proof or a claim of priority. I have not established whether these counterexamples have been reported previously.

Thank you to Zhi-Wei Sun and to the Formal Conjectures maintainers for making this conjecture available for systematic checking.
title: Counterexamples n=14 and n=286 to OEIS A238281 conjecture_2

## 1. Erdős Problem 142 — Missing Parameter $k$ in `answer` ([142.lean](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/142.lean#L34-L65))

### Current Code
```lean
def erdos_142.answer : ℕ → ℝ := sorry

@[category research open, question value, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_142 (k : ℕ) : (fun N => (r k N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_142.answer := by
  sorry

def erdos_142.variants.isTheta.answer : ℕ → ℝ := sorry

@[category research open, question value, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_142.variants.isTheta (k : ℕ) :
    (fun N => (r k N : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_142.variants.isTheta.answer := by
  sorry
```

### Defect
The docstrings state: *"find $f_k$ with $r_k(N) / f_k(N) \to 1$"* and *"find $f_k$ with $r_k(N) \asymp_k f_k(N)$"*. However, `erdos_142.answer` and `erdos_142.variants.isTheta.answer` are defined with type `ℕ → ℝ` (taking only $N$) instead of `ℕ → ℕ → ℝ` (taking $k$ and $N$). As written, the theorems require a single $k$-independent function of $N$ to be asymptotic to $r_k(N)$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ simultaneously—which is false (e.g., $r_1(N) = 0$, $r_2(N) = 1$, while $r_3(N) \to \infty$).

### Proposed Fix
```lean
def erdos_142.answer : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ := sorry

@[category research open, question value, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_142 (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 < k) :
    (fun N => (r k N : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_142.answer k := by
  sorry

def erdos_142.variants.isTheta.answer : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ := sorry

@[category research open, question value, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_142.variants.isTheta (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 < k) :
    (fun N => (r k N : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_142.variants.isTheta.answer k := by
  sorry
```

---

## 2. Erdős Problem 160 — Vacuous Quantifier Scoping in `better_lower` ([160.lean](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/160.lean#L71-L77))

### Current Code
```lean
@[category research open, question value, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.better_lower:
    (erdos_160.better_lower.answer =O[atTop] fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ c > 0,
    (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12))) =O[atTop] (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) →
    ∀ c > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12))) =o[atTop]
      erdos_160.better_lower.answer := by
  sorry
```

### Defect
In Lean 4, `∀ c > 0, P c → ∀ c > 0, Q c` parses as:
$$\forall c > 0,\ \big(P(c) \longrightarrow \forall c' > 0,\ Q(c')\big)$$
If one instead meant $\big(\forall c > 0,\, P(c)\big) \to \big(\forall c > 0,\, Q(c)\big)$, or meant that `better_lower.answer` strictly improves on the known Kelley–Meka lower bound $\exp(c (\log n)^{1/12})$ for whatever $c > 0$ satisfies the known bound (`erdos_160.variants.known_lower` only asserts $\exists c > 0,\, P(c)$), the current statement has two issues:
1. For any $c > 0$ where $P(c)$ fails, the implication $P(c) \to \dots$ holds vacuously.
2. Even for a $c_0 > 0$ where $P(c_0)$ holds, the consequent demands $\forall c' > 0,\ \exp(c' (\log n)^{1/12}) = o(\text{answer}(n))$ for arbitrarily large $c' > 0$ (e.g., requiring $\text{answer}(n)$ to beat $\exp(c (\log n)^{1/12})$ for *all* $c > 0$). If the intended meaning is to beat the specific $c > 0$ from `known_lower` (or to beat all $c > 0$ for which the bound holds), the second `∀ c > 0` should not re-quantify $c$.

### Proposed Fix
```lean
@[category research open, question value, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.better_lower :
    (erdos_160.better_lower.answer =O[atTop] fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ c > 0,
      (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12))) =O[atTop]
        (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) →
      (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12))) =o[atTop]
        erdos_160.better_lower.answer := by
  sorry
```

---

## 3. Erdős Problem 312 — Missing Positivity Constraint Allows Zero-Padding ([312.lean](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/312.lean#L36-L45))

### Current Code
```lean
@[category research open, question, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_312 :
    ∃ (c : ℝ), 0 < c ∧
      ∀ (K : ℝ), 1 < K →
        ∃ (N₀ : ℕ),
          ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → ℕ),
            (n ≥ N₀ ∧ (∑ i : Fin n, (a i : ℝ)⁻¹) > K) →
              ∃ (S : Finset (Fin n)),
                1 - Real.exp (-(c * K)) < (∑ i ∈ S, (a i : ℝ)⁻¹) ∧
                ∑ i ∈ S, (a i : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ 1 := by
  sorry
```

### Defect
The multiset elements `a : Fin n → ℕ` are not constrained to be positive (`∀ i, 0 < a i`). Because `(0 : ℝ)⁻¹ = 0` in Mathlib, any fixed small multiset of positive integers whose reciprocals sum to $> K$ (e.g., $2K$ copies of $2$, none of whose subset sums lie in $(1/2, 1)$) can be padded with $N_0$ zeros (`a i = 0`) to reach total length $n \ge N_0$ without changing $\sum (a_i)^{-1}$ or any subset sum $\sum_{i \in S} (a_i)^{-1}$. This completely neutralizes the `∃ N₀, ∀ n ≥ N₀` ("sufficiently large multiset") hypothesis and makes the theorem false as stated (for $K$ large enough that $\exp(-cK) < 1/2$, padding $2\lceil K\rceil$ copies of $2$ with zeros gives subset sums that are multiples of $1/2$, so no subset sum lies in $(1 - \exp(-cK), 1)$ except $1$ itself, or using copies of $3$ if needed).

### Proposed Fix
Add `(∀ i, 0 < a i)` to the hypothesis:
```lean
          ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → ℕ),
            (n ≥ N₀ ∧ (∀ i, 0 < a i) ∧ (∑ i : Fin n, (a i : ℝ)⁻¹) > K) →
```

---

## 4. Erdős Problem 319 — Constant `answer : ℕ` Instead of `ℕ → ℕ` ([319.lean](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/319.lean#L34-L79))

### Current Code
```lean
def erdos_319.answer : ℕ := sorry

@[category research open, question value, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_319 (N : ℕ) : IsGreatest
    { #A | (A) (_ : A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N)
      (_ : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℤˣ, ∑ n ∈ A, (δ n : ℚ) / n = 0 ∧
        ∀ A' ⊂ A, A'.Nonempty → ∑ n ∈ A', (δ n : ℚ) / n ≠ 0) }
    erdos_319.answer := by
  sorry
```

### Defect
1. `erdos_319.answer` has type `ℕ` instead of `ℕ → ℕ`. In `theorem erdos_319 (N : ℕ)`, this asserts that the maximum cardinality `#A` for $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ is the **same constant** `erdos_319.answer` for all $N \in \mathbb{N}$—contradicting `erdos_319.variants.lb`, which states the maximum grows at least as $(1 - 1/e + o(1))N$.
2. Additionally, in `theorem erdos_319.variants.isTheta (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) (h : ∀ N, ...)`, the parameter `(N : ℕ)` on line 73 is unused and shadowed by `∀ N`.

### Proposed Fix
```lean
def erdos_319.answer : ℕ → ℕ := sorry

@[category research open, question value, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_319 (N : ℕ) : IsGreatest
    { #A | (A) (_ : A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N)
      (_ : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℤˣ, ∑ n ∈ A, (δ n : ℚ) / n = 0 ∧
        ∀ A' ⊂ A, A'.Nonempty → ∑ n ∈ A', (δ n : ℚ) / n ≠ 0) }
    (erdos_319.answer N) := by
  sorry
```
*(And remove the unused `(N : ℕ)` parameter from `erdos_319.variants.isTheta` on line 73.)*

---

## 5. Erdős Problem 321 — Constant `answer : ℕ` Instead of `ℕ → ℕ` ([321.lean](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/321.lean#L42-L51))

### Current Code
```lean
def erdos_321.answer : ℕ := sorry

@[category research open, question value, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_321 (N : ℕ) :
    R N = erdos_321.answer := by
  sorry
```

### Defect
`erdos_321.answer` is typed as a constant `ℕ` instead of `ℕ → ℕ`, so `theorem erdos_321 (N : ℕ) : R N = erdos_321.answer` asserts that $R(N)$ is constant for all $N \in \mathbb{N}$ (which is immediately false since $R(0) = 0, R(1) = 1, R(2) = 2$, and $R(N) \ge \frac{N}{\log N} \prod_{i=3}^k \log_i N$).

### Proposed Fix
```lean
def erdos_321.answer : ℕ → ℕ := sorry

@[category research open, question value, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_321 (N : ℕ) :
    R N = erdos_321.answer N := by
  sorry
```

---

## 6. Erdős Problem 695 — Degenerate $k = 0$ Index in `upperBound` ([695.lean](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/695.lean#L54-L63))

### Current Code
```lean
@[category research open, question, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_695.variants.upperBound :
    ∃ q : ℕ → ℕ,
      StrictMono q ∧
      (∀ i, (q i).Prime) ∧
      (∀ i, q (i + 1) % q i = 1) ∧
      ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ,
        (o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)) ∧
        -- We use `(k + 1)` here as the informal statement is 1-indexed.
        ∀ k, q k ≤ exp ((k + 1) * log (k + 1) ^ (1 + o k)) := by
  sorry
```

### Defect
At $k = 0$, `(k + 1 : ℝ) = 1`, so `log (k + 1) = log 1 = 0`. For any $1 + o(0) \neq 0$, `0 ^ (1 + o 0) = 0` in Mathlib, making the right-hand side `exp 0 = 1`, which violates `q 0 ≤ 1` since `(q 0).Prime` requires `q 0 ≥ 2`. The only way the $k = 0$ inequality can hold in Lean is by artificially setting $o(0) = -1$ to exploit Mathlib's convention `(0 : ℝ) ^ (0 : ℝ) = 1` (yielding $q(0) \le \exp(1) \approx 2.718$, which also artificially forces $q(0) = 2$).

### Proposed Fix
Use `∀ᶠ k in atTop` (or guard `1 ≤ k`):
```lean
        ∀ᶠ k in atTop, (q k : ℝ) ≤ exp ((k + 1) * log (k + 1) ^ (1 + o k)) := by
```

---

## 7. Erdős Problem 1180 (and 1203) — All-Primes Quantifier vs. Large-Prime Threshold ([1180.lean](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1180.lean#L52-L107), [1203.lean](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1203.lean#L38-L40))

### Current Code ([1180.lean](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1180.lean#L52-L54))
```lean
noncomputable def C (ε : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {C | ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p, ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, s.card ≤ C ∧ Represents ε p a s}
```

### Defect
1. **In [1180.lean](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1180.lean#L52-L107):** As noted in the docstrings of `erdos_1180.variants.shparlinski` (lines 78–80) and `erdos_1180.variants.optimal` (lines 110–113):
   > *"Here $C_\epsilon$ is the number of summands needed for every sufficiently large prime... For all primes no such bound holds, since when $p^\epsilon < 2$ the only admissible denominator is $1$."*
   Because `def C (ε : ℝ)` quantifies over **all** primes `∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime` rather than `∃ P : ℕ, ∀ p ≥ P, p.Prime`, for every prime $p < 2^{1/\varepsilon}$ the only admissible denominator $1 \le n \le p^\varepsilon$ is $n = 1$, forcing $p - 1$ summands to represent $-1 \pmod p$. Consequently, `C ε` as defined satisfies $C(\varepsilon) \ge \max_{p < 2^{1/\varepsilon}} (p - 1) = \Omega(2^{1/\varepsilon})$, whereas `erdos_1180.variants.lower_bound` (lines 105–107) uses this all-primes `C ε` to state the polynomial lower bound $K \varepsilon^{-1} \le C(\varepsilon)$ intended for the asymptotic large-prime constant.
2. **In [1203.lean](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1203.lean#L38-L40):**
   ```lean
   noncomputable def F (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
     ⨆ k : ℕ, (ω (n + k) : ℝ) * (log (log (k : ℝ)) / log (k : ℝ))
   ```
   `k : ℕ` ranges over all naturals including $k \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, where $\log\log k / \log k$ is either $0/0 = 0$ ($k \in \{0, 1\}$) or negative ($k = 2$). While `⨆` over $\mathbb{N}$ still evaluates to the positive supremum achieved on $k \ge 3$, restricting the index to `⨆ k ≥ 3` (or `⨆ k : {k : ℕ // 3 ≤ k}`) matches the mathematical domain where $\log\log k > 0$.

### Proposed Fix ([1180.lean](file:///Users/anders/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/ocaml-agent-collab/erdos_analysis/formal-conjectures/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1180.lean#L52-L54))
Define an asymptotic large-prime constant `C_asymp` (or update `C`) using `∀ᶠ p in atTop`:
```lean
noncomputable def C_asymp (ε : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {C | ∀ᶠ p : ℕ in atTop, p.Prime → ∀ a : ZMod p,
    ∃ s : Multiset ℕ, s.card ≤ C ∧ Represents ε p a s}
```
title: Seven Unprovable or Vacuous Lean 4 Statements in Erdős #142, #160, #312, #319, #321, #695, #1180/#1203: Answer-Arity Omissions, Quantifier-Scope Vacuity, and Mathlib Junk-Value Loopholes

body:
https://github.com/BoltonBailey/formal-conjectures-ai-review tracks audits of statements in this repository. This issue is meant to be a landing page for the 10 top issues found by that audit effort in an ongoing way. As more audits come in which surface new problems or reassess fixed statements, this issue should update to reflect what the current high priority issues are.

---

- [x] `Erdos975.erdos_975.variants.quadratic`: severity 5, misformulated (provability differs) (fixed by [#8015](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/8015))

   <details>
   <summary>Details</summary>

   - **File:** [FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/975.lean](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/a919f7f47b836b766f378c2b1360b28168bbdd9d/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/975.lean)
   - **Commit:** [`a919f7f47b83`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/a919f7f47b836b766f378c2b1360b28168bbdd9d) (2026-11-13)
   - **Model:** claude-fable-5-2
   - **Audit file:** [Erdos975-erdos_975-variants-quadratic.json](https://github.com/BoltonBailey/formal-conjectures-ai-review/blob/main/audits/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/975/Erdos975-erdos_975-variants-quadratic.json)
   - **Other models:** claude-opus-5-5 severity 1

   Compared against erdosproblems.com/975: 'Such an asymptotic formula is known whenever f is an irreducible quadratic, as proved by Hooley. The form of c depends on f in a complicated fashion (see the work of McKee …)'. The Lean statement is: for every irreducible f of degree 2 with f(n) ≥ 1 eventually and every c, c = erdos_975.variants.quadratic.answer → 0 < c ∧ Erdos975Sum f x/(x log x) → c. The placeholder `answer : ℝ` is a single real number that does not depend on f, so the statement asserts that all irreducible quadratics share the same limiting constant. That is false: for f = X² + 1 the constant is 3/π (the file's own n2_plus_1_strong), whereas for other quadratics it is different (e.g. by McKee's class-number formula the constant for X² + 2 is 12·H(8)/(π√8) = 3√2/π ≠ 3/π). Hence no value of the answer makes the theorem true, and the declaration as stated is unprovable although the result it is meant to record (Hooley's theorem) is true. The answer needs to be a function of f (e.g. answer : ℤ[X] → ℝ), or the statement should be existential in c as in erdos_975.

   </details>

- [x] `Erdos503.erdos_503`: severity 5, misformulated (provability differs) (fixed by [#7946](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/7946))

   <details>
   <summary>Details</summary>

   - **File:** [FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/503.lean](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/a425ca3eb797fe927cb88c950565fdcbbbbada70/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/503.lean)
   - **Commit:** [`a425ca3eb797`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/a425ca3eb797fe927cb88c950565fdcbbbbada70) (2026-11-12)
   - **Model:** claude-fable-5-2
   - **Audit file:** [Erdos503-erdos_503.json](https://github.com/BoltonBailey/formal-conjectures-ai-review/blob/main/audits/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/503/Erdos503-erdos_503.json)
   - **Other models:** claude-opus-5-5 severity 1

   Compared against erdosproblems.com/503: 'What is the size of the largest A ⊆ R^d such that every three points from A determine an isosceles triangle?' — a quantity that depends on the dimension d (6 for d = 2, 8 for d = 3, between C(d+1,2)+1 and C(d+2,2) in general). In the Lean file the answer is declared as a single natural number, 'def erdos_503.answer : ℕ := sorry', while the theorem is 'theorem erdos_503 (n : ℕ) : IsGreatest {A.ncard | A : Set (ℝ^n), A.IsIsosceles} erdos_503.answer', universally quantified over the dimension n. No value of the constant can satisfy this for all n: the file's own solved variants erdos_503.variants.R2 and erdos_503.variants.R3 state that the greatest element is 6 for n = 2 and 8 for n = 3 (and for n = 0 it is 1), and IsGreatest determines its value uniquely. So the statement as written is false for every choice of erdos_503.answer and cannot express the intended problem. The intended form is an answer depending on the dimension, e.g. 'def erdos_503.answer : ℕ → ℕ := sorry' with conclusion 'IsGreatest {...} (erdos_503.answer n)'. The rest of the encoding (Set.IsIsosceles = nonempty and every triple of distinct points has two equal distances; ncard; ℝ^n as Euclidean space) is fine.

   </details>

- [x] `Erdos506.erdos_506`: severity 5, misformulated (provability differs) (fixed by [#7946](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/7946))

   <details>
   <summary>Details</summary>

   - **File:** [FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/506.lean](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/da703a5f239f734a47ede2f4e99b9ccc9e644cb5/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/506.lean)
   - **Commit:** [`da703a5f239f`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/da703a5f239f734a47ede2f4e99b9ccc9e644cb5) (2026-11-11)
   - **Model:** claude-fable-5-2
   - **Audit file:** [Erdos506-erdos_506.json](https://github.com/BoltonBailey/formal-conjectures-ai-review/blob/main/audits/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/506/Erdos506-erdos_506.json)
   - **Other models:** claude-opus-5-5 severity 1

   Compared against erdosproblems.com/506: 'What is the minimum number of circles determined by any n points in ℝ², not all on a circle?' — a value question whose answer is a function of n (for n > 393 it is C(n−1,2) + 1 − ⌊(n−1)/2⌋ by Elliott with the Purdy–Smith correction). Concrete defect: the Lean unknown is declared as `def erdos_506.answer : ℕ := sorry`, a single natural number independent of n, while the theorem asserts, for every n ≥ 4, IsLeast {numCircles P : |P| = n, P not collinear, not cospherical} erdos_506.answer. Since the minimum changes with n — e.g. the file's own large_n variant gives 76833 for n = 394 and 77225 for n = 395 — no single natural number can be the least element for all n, so the statement is false for every choice of answer and can never be 'solved' as intended. The answer should have type ℕ → ℕ (as erdos_506.variants.large_n.answer does). The same defect affects erdos_506.variants.small_n (constant answer for all 4 ≤ n ≤ 393). The rest (numCircles, non-degeneracy assumptions, n ≥ 4) is reasonable.

   </details>

- [ ] `Erdos525.erdos_525.parts.ii`: severity 5, misformulated (provability differs)

   <details>
   <summary>Details</summary>

   - **File:** [FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/525.lean](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/2f91d251c07fbbaf9435166d47c11e884a08a6cf/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/525.lean)
   - **Commit:** [`2f91d251c07f`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/2f91d251c07fbbaf9435166d47c11e884a08a6cf) (2026-11-09)
   - **Model:** claude-fable-5-2
   - **Audit file:** [Erdos525-erdos_525-parts-ii.json](https://github.com/BoltonBailey/formal-conjectures-ai-review/blob/main/audits/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/525/Erdos525-erdos_525-parts-ii.json)

   Compared against erdosproblems.com/525 and the cited paper, Cook–Nguyen, 'Universality of the minimum modulus for random trigonometric polynomials' (Discrete Analysis 2021:20, arXiv:2101.07203v3). The site only says lim P(m(f) > ε n^{-1/2}) = e^{-ελ} 'where λ is an explicit constant'; the Lean statement fixes λ = √(π/12), and this value appears to be wrong by a factor of 2. In the paper (eqs. (1.4)–(1.6), Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.5, which covers Rademacher signs) the normalised polynomial is P_n(x) = (2n+1)^{-1/2} Σ_{j=-n}^{n} ξ_j e(jx), m_n = min|P_n|, and lim P(m_n > τ/n) = e^{-λτ} with λ = 2√(π/3). Up to a unimodular factor P_n is (2n+1)^{-1/2} F_{2n}, so for the degree N = 2n polynomial f = F_N of the Lean statement, m_n > τ/n means m(f) > τ√(2n+1)/n ≈ 2τ/√N. Putting ε = 2τ gives lim P(m(f) > ε/√N) = e^{-2√(π/3)·ε/2} = e^{-√(π/3) ε}, i.e. λ = √(π/3) ≈ 1.023 in the site's normalisation, not √(π/12) ≈ 0.512. (A first-moment count of near-zeros agrees: the expected number of passes of the curve within δ of 0 is δ√N·√(π/3); √(π/12) arises only as an intermediate quantity, E|P_n'|/n.) Since the limit e^{-√(π/12) ε} differs from the true limit e^{-√(π/3) ε} for every ε > 0, the Lean statement as written is false. The rest of the formalisation (uniform ±1 coefficients on Fin (n+1), m as the infimum of |f| over the unit circle, `prob` as a normalised count) is fine; I did not find the constant √(π/12) in the paper for this normalisation, and the `formal_proof` link is the same line as for part (i), so it does not appear to certify this statement.

   </details>

- [x] `Erdos552.erdos_552.parts.i`: severity 5, misformulated (provability differs) (fixed by [#7946](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/7946))

   <details>
   <summary>Details</summary>

   - **File:** [FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/552.lean](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/2f91d251c07fbbaf9435166d47c11e884a08a6cf/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/552.lean)
   - **Commit:** [`2f91d251c07f`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/2f91d251c07fbbaf9435166d47c11e884a08a6cf) (2026-11-09)
   - **Model:** claude-fable-5-2
   - **Audit file:** [Erdos552-erdos_552-parts-i.json](https://github.com/BoltonBailey/formal-conjectures-ai-review/blob/main/audits/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/552/Erdos552-erdos_552-parts-i.json)
   - **Other models:** claude-opus-5-5 severity 1

   Compared against erdosproblems.com/552 ("Determine the Ramsey number R(C_4,S_n), where S_n=K_{1,n}"). The intended object is a function of n, but the unknown is declared as a single number `erdos_552.parts.i.answer : ℕ` that does not take n as a parameter, and the statement is `∀ n, graphRamsey C_4 K_{1,n} = erdos_552.parts.i.answer`. This asserts that R(C_4,S_n) is the same for every n, which is false: the site records n+√n−6n^{11/40} ≤ R(C_4,S_n), so the values are unbounded (and the file's own docstring for `succ_le_add_two` notes R(C_4,S_0)=1 ≠ 4=R(C_4,S_1)). So the statement is false for every possible value of the answer, and no determination of R(C_4,S_n) could prove it. The upstream CONTRIBUTING.md says the answer definition should take the theorem's parameters when the unknown depends on them; the fix is `answer : ℕ → ℕ` applied to n. The graphs themselves (cycleGraph 4, completeBipartiteGraph (Fin 1) (Fin n), graphRamsey as least N such that every graph on Fin N contains C_4 or has K_{1,n} in its complement) are a correct rendering.

   </details>

- [ ] `Arxiv.«2406.10319».pittel_hyperbola_threshold`: severity 4, essentially misformalized

   <details>
   <summary>Details</summary>

   - **File:** [FormalConjectures/Arxiv/2406.10319/StableMatchingHyperbola.lean](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/a919f7f47b836b766f378c2b1360b28168bbdd9d/FormalConjectures/Arxiv/2406.10319/StableMatchingHyperbola.lean)
   - **Commit:** [`a919f7f47b83`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/a919f7f47b836b766f378c2b1360b28168bbdd9d) (2026-11-13)
   - **Model:** claude-fable-5-2
   - **Audit file:** [Arxiv-«2406-10319»-pittel_hyperbola_threshold.json](https://github.com/BoltonBailey/formal-conjectures-ai-review/blob/main/audits/FormalConjectures/Arxiv/2406.10319/StableMatchingHyperbola/Arxiv-«2406-10319»-pittel_hyperbola_threshold.json)

   Compared against B. Pittel, 'On Constrained Matchings, Stable Under Random Preferences' (arXiv:2406.10319, p. 26, Notes (2)). The source conjecture is a single informal sentence: 'We conjecture existence of p*(n) ∈ [9/4·log²n/n, 1], a critical threshold for appearance of a hyperbolic curve, as an asymptotic approximation of {(Q(M), R(M))}_M.' The underlying model is formalized faithfully: uniform independent preferences, each pair admissible independently with probability p (marketLaw), Gusfield–Irving stability of partial matchings (IsPartialStable), and Q, R as total ranks among admissible partners (totalWifeRank/totalHusbandRank), all as in the paper. However, the paper gives no precise meaning to 'critical threshold' or 'appearance of a hyperbolic curve', and the Lean statement supplies one through several choices that are not in the source: (a) the scaling of both ranks by √(p n³) (natural, since Theorem 1.6 gives Q ≈ R ≈ (pn³)^{1/2} below log²n/n and QR ≈ n³ at p = 1, but not stated by Pittel for intermediate p); (b) 'hyperbola appears' is defined as: every stable M has |qr − 1| ≤ ε and the fixed arc {(t, 1/t) : t ∈ [2/3, 3/2]} is ε-covered; the arc endpoints are arbitrary, and the threshold for covering this particular arc need not be the threshold at which a nondegenerate curve first appears (by Theorem 1.7, Q⁻ ≥ (1−ε) n log n for c > 9/4, so t = 2/3 can only be reached when c is about 9/4 or more, which makes the choice of arc effectively decide the location of p*); (c) the threshold is required to be sharp in a strong sense, with a relative window δ·min(p*, 1 − p*) and uniformity over all p outside the window, whereas the source's 'critical threshold' could also be coarse; (d) p* is restricted to the open interval (0,1) with a strict eventual lower bound, while the source allows the closed interval. Each choice is reasonable and the docstring documents them, but the resulting statement is one specific strengthening/interpretation among many, and its truth could differ from what Pittel intends (e.g. if the transition is not sharp in this relative sense, or if a hyperbolic arc of smaller extent appears earlier). So it is unclear that this is a correct formulation of the conjecture; the source is arguably too vague to formalize canonically.

   </details>

- [ ] `Erdos422.erdos_422.variants.growth_rate`: severity 4, essentially misformalized

   <details>
   <summary>Details</summary>

   - **File:** [FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/422.lean](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/a919f7f47b836b766f378c2b1360b28168bbdd9d/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/422.lean)
   - **Commit:** [`a919f7f47b83`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/a919f7f47b836b766f378c2b1360b28168bbdd9d) (2026-11-13)
   - **Model:** claude-fable-5-2
   - **Audit file:** [Erdos422-erdos_422-variants-growth_rate.json](https://github.com/BoltonBailey/formal-conjectures-ai-review/blob/main/audits/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/422/Erdos422-erdos_422-variants-growth_rate.json)

   Compared against erdosproblems.com/422, whose second question is the vague 'What is its behaviour?'. The Lean statement is ∀ f, IsHofstadterQ f → (n ↦ f n) =O[atTop] answer with answer : ℕ+ → ℝ to be supplied. This asks only for an upper bound, and one is immediate from the definition: IsHofstadterQ requires f(n−1) < n for all n > 2, so f(m) ≤ m for all m and answer := (fun n ↦ n) makes the statement provable in a few lines (the conjectured truth f(n) ~ n/2 gives nothing better at the level of O). So although tagged 'research open', the statement as written is not an open problem and does not capture 'how does f grow' (which would need at least a Θ or asymptotic statement). The upstream convention says meaningfulness of answers is out of scope, but here the one-sided O makes the canonical trivial answer also the sharp one, so the formalisation does not correspond to an open question.

   </details>

- [ ] `Erdos897.erdos_897.variants.log_growth`: severity 4, essentially misformalized

   <details>
   <summary>Details</summary>

   - **File:** [FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/897.lean](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/a919f7f47b836b766f378c2b1360b28168bbdd9d/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/897.lean)
   - **Commit:** [`a919f7f47b83`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/a919f7f47b836b766f378c2b1360b28168bbdd9d) (2026-11-13)
   - **Model:** claude-fable-5-2
   - **Audit file:** [Erdos897-erdos_897-variants-log_growth.json](https://github.com/BoltonBailey/formal-conjectures-ai-review/blob/main/audits/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/897/Erdos897-erdos_897-variants-log_growth.json)

   Compared against erdosproblems.com/897: 'Wirsing [Wi70] proved (see [491]) that if |f(n+1) − f(n)| ≤ C then f(n) = c log n + O(1) for some constant c.' The Lean statement concludes only ∃ c, ∃ O with O =O[atTop] 1 and ∀ n, f n ≤ c·log n + O n — an inequality, i.e. a one-sided upper bound f(n) ≤ c log n + O(1), where the theorem asserts the two-sided f(n) = c log n + O(1). The one-sided statement is strictly weaker (for instance it does not exclude f(n) − c log n → −∞, and when it holds for some c > 0 it holds for every larger c), so it does not express Wirsing's characterisation. The sibling declaration Erdos491.erdos_491 states the result correctly as (n ↦ f n − c·log n) =O[atTop] 1, and the docstring here claims the linked formal proof 'gives this statement', which is true only in the sense that the correct theorem implies this weaker one. The ≤ should be =.

   </details>

- [ ] `DiophantineTuple.hasUniqueExtension_of_forall`: severity 4, essentially misformalized

   <details>
   <summary>Details</summary>

   - **File:** [FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/DiophantineTuple.lean](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/7bdc4a42f24c0316f81c73b26121794b2bed96a3/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/DiophantineTuple.lean)
   - **Commit:** [`7bdc4a42f24c`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/7bdc4a42f24c0316f81c73b26121794b2bed96a3) (2026-11-02)
   - **Model:** claude-opus-5-5
   - **Audit file:** [DiophantineTuple-hasUniqueExtension_of_forall.json](https://github.com/BoltonBailey/formal-conjectures-ai-review/blob/main/audits/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/DiophantineTuple/DiophantineTuple-hasUniqueExtension_of_forall.json)

   The strong Diophantine quintuple conjecture: every Diophantine triple {a, b, c} has at most one extension by d > max(a, b, c), namely the regular one. Because 0 is allowed in the definition, the triple {0, 1, 3} is "Diophantine" (products plus one: 1, 1, 4). It has two extensions with d > 3: d = 8 and d = 120, since d + 1 and 3d + 1 are both squares. Hence HasUniqueExtensionOfForall is false as formalized and the open conjecture is trivially disproved. Excluding 0 from the definition repairs it.

   </details>

- [ ] `DiophantineTuple.noIntegralDiophantineFiveTuple`: severity 4, essentially misformalized

   <details>
   <summary>Details</summary>

   - **File:** [FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/DiophantineTuple.lean](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/7bdc4a42f24c0316f81c73b26121794b2bed96a3/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/DiophantineTuple.lean)
   - **Commit:** [`7bdc4a42f24c`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/7bdc4a42f24c0316f81c73b26121794b2bed96a3) (2026-11-02)
   - **Model:** claude-opus-5-5
   - **Audit file:** [DiophantineTuple-noIntegralDiophantineFiveTuple.json](https://github.com/BoltonBailey/formal-conjectures-ai-review/blob/main/audits/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/DiophantineTuple/DiophantineTuple-noIntegralDiophantineFiveTuple.json)

   Intended as the He–Togbé–Ziegler theorem (no Diophantine quintuple of positive integers). However, IsDiophantineTuple does not exclude 0, even though its docstring says "each element is nonzero" and IsIntegralDiophantineTuple claims to be about positive integers. Since 0·x + 1 = 1 is a square, {0, 1, 3, 8, 120} is an IsIntegralDiophantineTuple of cardinality 5 (I verified all ten products numerically). So NoIntegralDiophantineFiveTuple is false as formalized, and this "research solved" theorem is unprovable. Fix: add x ≠ 0 (or 0 < x) to the definition.

   </details>

https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/HardyLittlewood.lean#L36-L41

The description of IsPrimeConstellation appears accurate.  The definition appears to inaccurately double the entry "m_i" in order to get an even number.
Lines 41 & 48 have: "p + 2 * m i"

### Trivial proof/disproof
Say we want the pattern p, p+2, p+6...where p=5.
Would result in:
|Position i| Entry m_i| Description's process| Code's process|
|---|---|---|---|
|0| 0| 5+0=5| 5+0=5 (no issues)|
|1| 2| 5+2=7| 5+4 (2*2) = *9*|
|2| 6| 5+6=11| 5+12 (6*2) =*17*|

### Suggested fix
Change the  code to "p + m i" on lines 41 and 48 and add a condition that each m_i is even next to the condition that says it is positive.

### Additional context
It could also be that the description is out of date and needs to change to match the code.  Either would make it agree.
I think the change is an improvement in that the current requirement is that the offsets have to be halved before storing them as m_i in order to make the code work as written ... which when looking at that process is not as intuitive.

body:
### Describe the misformalization

Since #7327, the unknown in each of these statements is a closed constant, but it sits under binders it has to depend on, so both statements are false whatever the answer is.

- [`erdos_450`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/c6f4b4bdab8fdabb19191a8a1648be21b81253b0/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/450.lean#L52-L65): `erdos_450.answer : ℕ∞` is used for every `ε` and `n`, but the problem asks for $y(\varepsilon, n)$ (#5786 made the statement ask for `windowThreshold ε n` itself). For each $n \ge 2$, `windowThreshold 1 n = 0`, while `windowThreshold (1/10) n > n`, because the $n - 1$ integers in $(n, 2n)$ are their own divisors in $(n, 2n)$.
- [`erdos_552.parts.i`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/c6f4b4bdab8fdabb19191a8a1648be21b81253b0/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/552.lean#L36-L53): `erdos_552.parts.i.answer : ℕ` is used for every `n`, but $R(C_4, K_{1,n})$ depends on $n$: it is 1 at $n = 0$ and 4 at $n = 1$ (both quoted in the file), and at least $n + 1$ in general.

### Trivial proof/disproof

Both negations compile against c6f4b4b. I wrote them with Claude; `#print axioms` shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`, plus `sorryAx` from the answer placeholder once they are applied to the repository's statements.

<details><summary>Erdős 450</summary>

```lean
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«450»

open Erdos450

namespace Erdos450Check

theorem threshold_zero (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : windowThreshold ε 0 = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (by simp)
  refine iInf_le_of_le ⟨0, fun z _ x => ?_⟩ (by simp)
  have h : localCount 0 x z = 0 := by
    classical
    unfold localCount
    convert Finset.card_empty (α := ℕ)
    exact Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff.2 fun m _ ⟨d, h1, h2, _⟩ => by omega
  rw [h, Nat.cast_zero]
  positivity

theorem threshold_two_ne_zero : windowThreshold (1 / 10) 2 ≠ 0 := by
  intro h
  have hle : (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ windowThreshold (1 / 10) 2 := by
    refine le_iInf fun ⟨y, hy⟩ => ?_
    by_contra hlt
    have hy1 : (y : ℕ∞) < 1 := not_le.1 hlt
    have hy0 : y < 1 := by exact_mod_cast hy1
    have hs := hy 3 (by omega) 2
    have hpos : 0 < localCount 2 2 3 := by
      classical
      unfold localCount
      exact Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨3, Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨by simp, 3, by norm_num, by norm_num, dvd_refl 3⟩⟩
    have h1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ localCount 2 2 3 := by exact_mod_cast hpos
    norm_num at hs
    linarith
  rw [h] at hle
  exact absurd hle (by norm_num)

/-- No constant equals the window threshold for every ε > 0 and every n. -/
theorem no_constant_threshold (a : ℕ∞) :
    ¬ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ n : ℕ, windowThreshold ε n = a := by
  intro h
  have h0 := h (1 / 10) (by norm_num) 0
  have h2 := h (1 / 10) (by norm_num) 2
  rw [threshold_zero _ (by norm_num)] at h0
  exact threshold_two_ne_zero (h2.trans h0.symm)

/-- The repository statement `erdos_450`, exactly as stated, is false (whatever the answer is). -/
theorem erdos_450_is_false : ¬ type_of% @Erdos450.erdos_450 :=
  no_constant_threshold _

end Erdos450Check
```
</details>

<details><summary>Erdős 552 (i)</summary>

```lean
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«552»

open SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos552Check

abbrev C4 := SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4
abbrev S (n : ℕ) := completeBipartiteGraph (Fin 1) (Fin n)

/-- A copy needs an injective map of vertex types. -/
theorem card_le_of_isContained {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] {G : SimpleGraph α}
    {H : SimpleGraph β} (h : G.IsContained H) : Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card β := by
  obtain ⟨c⟩ := h
  exact Fintype.card_le_of_injective c.toHom c.injective

theorem one_mem_S0 : ∀ C : SimpleGraph (Fin 1), C4.IsContained C ∨ (S 0).IsContained Cᶜ := by
  intro C
  right
  refine ⟨⟨⟨fun _ => 0, ?_⟩, ?_⟩⟩
  · intro a b hab
    rcases a with a | a <;> rcases b with b | b
    · simp at hab
    · exact b.elim0
    · exact a.elim0
    · exact a.elim0
  · intro a b _
    rcases a with a | a <;> rcases b with b | b
    · simp [Subsingleton.elim a b]
    · exact b.elim0
    · exact a.elim0
    · exact a.elim0

theorem R_S0 : graphRamsey C4 (S 0) = 1 := by
  have h1 : 1 ∈ {n : ℕ | ∀ (C : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), C4.IsContained C ∨ (S 0).IsContained Cᶜ} :=
    one_mem_S0
  apply le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le h1)
  rw [Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero]
  intro h0
  have hmem := Nat.sInf_mem ⟨1, h1⟩
  rw [h0] at hmem
  rcases hmem ⊥ with h | h
  · have := card_le_of_isContained h; simp at this
  · have := card_le_of_isContained h; simp at this

theorem R_S2_ne_one : graphRamsey C4 (S 2) ≠ 1 := by
  intro h1
  have hne : {n : ℕ | ∀ (C : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), C4.IsContained C ∨ (S 2).IsContained Cᶜ}.Nonempty := by
    by_contra hemp
    rw [Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty] at hemp
    have h1' : sInf {n : ℕ | ∀ (C : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), C4.IsContained C ∨ (S 2).IsContained Cᶜ} = 1 := h1
    rw [hemp, Nat.sInf_empty] at h1'
    exact absurd h1' (by norm_num)
  have hmem := Nat.sInf_mem hne
  have h1' : sInf {n : ℕ | ∀ (C : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), C4.IsContained C ∨ (S 2).IsContained Cᶜ} = 1 := h1
  rw [h1'] at hmem
  rcases hmem ⊥ with h | h
  · have := card_le_of_isContained h; simp at this
  · have := card_le_of_isContained h; simp at this

/-- No constant equals R(C₄, K_{1,n}) for every n. -/
theorem no_constant (a : ℕ) : ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, graphRamsey C4 (S n) = a := by
  intro h
  exact R_S2_ne_one ((h 2).trans ((h 0).symm.trans R_S0))

/-- The repository statement `erdos_552.parts.i`, exactly as stated, is false. -/
theorem erdos_552_parts_i_is_false : ¬ type_of% @Erdos552.erdos_552.parts.i :=
  no_constant _

end Erdos552Check
```
</details>

### Suggested fix

Make each answer a function of what it depends on, as CONTRIBUTING.md now asks and as #5840 did for `green_24`:
- `def erdos_450.answer : ℝ → ℕ → ℕ∞ := sorry`, with `windowThreshold ε n = erdos_450.answer ε n`;
- `def erdos_552.parts.i.answer : ℕ → ℕ := sorry`, with `... = erdos_552.parts.i.answer n`.

### Additional context

The same defect elsewhere: #7434 (`erdos_409.parts.i`, also after #7327) and #5446 (other files, before #7327).

- [x] This issue is up for grabs: I would like to see this misformalization fixed by somebody else

`FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor` in `FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/HardyLittlewood.lean:63` defines `C_P` with `∏' q : {q // q.Prime ∧ 3 ≤ q}`.

Same defect class as #5255: `∏'` is `tprod`, unconditional. Junk `1` if not `Multipliable`. Here log-factor is `O(1/q)`, `∑ 1/p` diverges, so product is conditionally convergent only in increasing-prime order. Formal constant is `0` or junk.

Permalink: `FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/HardyLittlewood.lean#L63`
Related: #5255 (Bateman-Horn), #4996 (covers =O vs ∼, not this product)

### Trivial proof/disproof
No full disproof yet, by analogy to #5255 disproof (`X²+1` vs `4X²+1` giving same `1/2`): any two constellations with same `k` but different true constants will get same junk value here.

### Suggested fix
Same as #5255: replace with `N ↦ ∏ q in Nat.primesBelow N, ...` and state `∃ C > 0, Tendsto ... (𝓝 C) ∧ ...`, or otherwise make order explicit.

`ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.lean:63` checked — `1/p(p-1)` is summable, `∏'` valid there. Only Hardy-Littlewood needs fix among the `∏'` hits.

### Additional context
Found by `grep ∏'` audit (5 hits). `lake` build not run locally — statement-only change.

- [X] I plan on working on this issue

### Describe the misformalization
In Erdos 124, there are is a missing hypothesis that allows for a "proof" via junk values.
- The real-valued tsum bound does not require the reciprocal series to converge

Also there is a mismatch in the docstring and statement
- StrictMono d does not imply the docstring’s requirement 2 ≤ d 0

[Permalink](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/e99b54b6d8084a8df4e889c8023b1270a0f3e683/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/124.lean#L99-L104)

### Trivial proof/disproof
```
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
lemma erdos124.melfi_construction {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ d : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono d ∧ ∑' i, (d i - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ ε ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ (I : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ i ∈ I, a i ∈ sumsOfDistinctPowers (d i) 0) ∧
        ∑ i ∈ I, a i = n := by
  -- Junk-value loophole: with `d i = i + 2` the series `∑ (d i - 1)⁻¹ = ∑ (i + 1)⁻¹`
  -- diverges, so `tsum` returns `0 ≤ ε`; and every `n` is a sum of distinct powers of
  -- `d 0 = 2`. Melfi's construction is not needed.
  refine ⟨fun i => i + 2, fun _ _ hab => Nat.add_lt_add_right hab 2, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have h : ¬ Summable (fun i : ℕ => ((i + 2 : ℕ) - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹) := by
      have h' : (fun i : ℕ => ((i + 2 : ℕ) - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹) =
          fun i : ℕ => ((i + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
        funext i
        push_cast
        ring
      rw [h']
      intro hs
      exact Real.not_summable_natCast_inv
        ((summable_nat_add_iff (f := fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)⁻¹) 1).mp hs)
    rw [tsum_eq_zero_of_not_summable h]
    exact hε.le
  · refine Eventually.of_forall fun n => ⟨{0}, fun _ => n, ?_, by simp⟩
    intro i hi
    rw [Finset.mem_singleton] at hi
    subst hi
    exact ⟨n.bitIndices.toFinset, fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _,
      Finset.sum_toFinset_bitIndices_two_pow n⟩
```

### Suggested fix
Add hypotheses `2 ≤ d 0` and  `Summable (fun i : ℕ ↦ (d i - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹)`

### Additional context
Found by a junk value audit of the repository. Also found in the fc-review audit: https://tadamcz.com/fc-review-results/#/f/ErdosProblems/124

### Choose either option
- [x] I plan on working on this issue
title: Erdős 124: missing summability hypothesis and docstring mismatch in melfi_construction
