<summary>The accepted Lean proof</summary>

```lean
import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Bloch and Landau constants

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloch%27s_theorem_(complex_analysis))
- [CP96] Chen, H., Gauthier, P. M. "On Bloch's constant." Journal d'Analyse Mathématique 69 (1996),
  275–291.
- [AG37] Ahlfors, L. V., Grunsky, H. "Über die Blochsche Konstante." Mathematische Zeitschrift 42
  (1937), 671–673.
- [Ya95] Yanagihara, H. "On the locally univalent Bloch constant." Journal d'Analyse Mathématique
  65 (1995), 1–17.
- [Ra43] Rademacher, H. "On the Bloch-Landau Constant."" American Journal of Mathematics 65 (1943),
  387–390.
- [OptimizationConstants](https://teorth.github.io/optimizationproblems/constants/57c.html)
- [Skin2009] Skinner, Brian. The univalent Bloch constant problem. Complex Variables and Elliptic
  Equations 54 (2009), no. 10, 951–955.
- [MathWorld](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/BlochConstant.html)
- [Bhowmik–Sen](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/canadian-mathematical-bulletin/article/improved-bloch-and-landau-constants-for-meromorphic-functions/FD465D1F2CEF7E8C62AFF16C3E89B7B4)
-/
open scoped Topology ENNReal
open Metric Set Filter
namespace Bloch

/-- The **Bloch radius** $B_f$ of a function $f$ is the supremum of radii of univalent disks in the
image of the unit disk under $f$. Takes values in `ℝ≥0∞` so that functions whose image contains
arbitrarily large univalent disks correctly get radius `⊤` rather than `0`. -/
noncomputable def blochRadius (f : ℂ → ℂ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sSup (ENNReal.ofReal '' {r : ℝ | ∃ S ⊆ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, ∃ x, ball x r ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S})

/-- The **Landau radius** $L_f$ of a function $f$ is the supremum of radii of disks contained in
the image of the unit disk under $f$. Takes values in `ℝ≥0∞` so that functions with unbounded
image correctly get radius `⊤`. -/
noncomputable def landauRadius (f : ℂ → ℂ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sSup (ENNReal.ofReal '' {r : ℝ | ∃ x, ball x r ⊆ f '' (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)})

/-- The **Bloch constant** $B$ is the largest radius such that every holomorphic function on the
unit disk with $f'(0) = 1$ has a schlicht (univalent) disk of that radius in its image. -/
noncomputable def blochConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) → deriv f 0 = 1 →
    ∃ S ⊆ ball 0 1, ∃ x, ball x B ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S}

/-
The definition above differs from the classical Bloch constant: `S` need not be open.
Consequently, any disk in the image admits an injective set of preimages by choice.
We use Landau's estimate to obtain the lower bound `49 / 100` for this definition,
and show that the proposed gamma expression is strictly smaller.
-/
namespace Aux

open scoped ComplexConjugate

/-- A local form of the Schwarz metric comparison, proved by the maximum modulus principle. -/
lemma local_schwarz (g : ℂ → ℂ) (hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g 0) (hzero : g 0 = 0)
    (hmax : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 (0 : ℂ),
      (1 - ‖z‖^2) * ‖deriv g z‖ ≤ ‖deriv g 0‖ * (1 - ‖g z‖^2)) :
    ‖deriv g 0‖ ≤ 1 := by
  by_contra hn
  have hn : 1 < ‖deriv g 0‖ := lt_of_not_ge hn
  have hsl := hg.differentiableAt.hasDerivAt.tendsto_slope.norm.eventually
    (lt_mem_nhds hn)
  have hstrict : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] (0 : ℂ), ‖deriv g z‖ < ‖deriv g 0‖ := by
    filter_upwards [hsl, hmax.filter_mono nhdsWithin_le_nhds,
      nhdsWithin_le_nhds (ball_mem_nhds (0 : ℂ) (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1)), self_mem_nhdsWithin] with z hsl hm hz hne
    have hz0 : z ≠ 0 := hne
    simp only [slope, hzero, sub_zero, smul_eq_mul, norm_mul, norm_inv] at hsl
    have hzg : ‖z‖ < ‖g z‖ := by
      have hzpos := norm_pos_iff.mpr hz0
      rw [← div_eq_inv_mul, lt_div_iff₀ hzpos] at hsl
      simpa using hsl
    have hz1 : ‖z‖ < 1 := by simpa using hz
    have hs : ‖z‖ ^ 2 < ‖g z‖ ^ 2 := by nlinarith [norm_nonneg z, norm_nonneg (g z)]
    have hw : 0 < 1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2 := by nlinarith [norm_nonneg z]
    nlinarith [norm_nonneg (deriv g 0)]
  have hlocal : IsLocalMax (norm ∘ deriv g) 0 := by
    have h' := eventually_nhdsWithin_iff.mp hstrict
    filter_upwards [h'] with z hz
    by_cases he : z = 0
    · simp [he]
    · exact (hz he).le
  have heq := Complex.norm_eventually_eq_of_isLocalMax
    (hg.deriv.eventually_analyticAt.mono fun _ h ↦ h.differentiableAt) hlocal
  obtain ⟨z, hz1, hz2⟩ := (hstrict.and (heq.filter_mono nhdsWithin_le_nhds)).exists
  exact hz1.ne hz2

lemma cayley_norm (c : ℝ) (z : ℂ) (h : (2*c : ℂ) - z ≠ 0) :
    1 - ‖z / ((2*c : ℂ) - z)‖^2 =
      4*c*(c-z.re) / ‖(2*c : ℂ) - z‖^2 := by
  rw [norm_div, div_pow]
  rw [sub_div' (pow_ne_zero 2 (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr h))]
  congr 1
  simp [Complex.sq_norm, Complex.normSq_apply]
  ring

lemma halfplane_local (q : ℂ → ℂ) (hq : AnalyticAt ℂ q 0) (hq0 : q 0 = 0)
    (c M : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (hM : ‖deriv q 0‖ = M*c)
    (hm : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 (0 : ℂ),
      (1-‖z‖^2) * ‖deriv q z‖ ≤ M * (c - (q z).re)) : M ≤ 2 := by
  let g : ℂ → ℂ := fun z ↦ q z / ((2*c : ℂ) - q z)
  have hden0 : (2*c : ℂ) - q 0 ≠ 0 := by simp [hq0, hc.ne']
  have hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g 0 := hq.div (analyticAt_const.sub hq) hden0
  have hg0 : g 0 = 0 := by simp [g, hq0]
  have hd : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 (0 : ℂ),
      ‖deriv g z‖ = 2*c*‖deriv q z‖ / ‖(2*c : ℂ) - q z‖^2 := by
    filter_upwards [hq.eventually_analyticAt,
      (continuousAt_const.sub hq.continuousAt).eventually_ne hden0] with z hz hden
    have hder := hz.differentiableAt.hasDerivAt.div
      ((hasDerivAt_const z (2*c : ℂ)).sub hz.differentiableAt.hasDerivAt) hden
    have hdg : deriv g z = (2*c : ℂ) * deriv q z / ((2*c : ℂ) - q z)^2 := by
      change HasDerivAt g _ z at hder
      rw [hder.deriv]
      dsimp only [Pi.sub_apply]
      congr 1
      ring
    rw [hdg, norm_div, norm_mul, norm_pow]
    norm_cast
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (by positivity : 0 < 2*c)]
  have hd0 : ‖deriv g 0‖ = M/2 := by
    have h := hd.self_of_nhds
    simp only [hq0, sub_zero] at h
    norm_cast at h
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (by positivity : 0 < 2*c), hM] at h
    rw [h]
    field_simp
  have hb := local_schwarz g hg hg0 (by
    filter_upwards [hm, hd,
      (continuousAt_const.sub hq.continuousAt).eventually_ne hden0] with z hm hd hden
    rw [hd, hd0]
    simp only [g]
    rw [cayley_norm c (q z) hden]
    have hdenpos : 0 < ‖(2*c : ℂ) - q z‖^2 := pow_pos (norm_pos_iff.mpr hden) _
    rw [← mul_div_assoc, ← mul_div_assoc, div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hdenpos]
    nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hm (by positivity : 0 ≤ 2*c)])
  rw [hd0] at hb
  linarith

/-- The reciprocal of the cusp metric used in Landau's estimate. -/
noncomputable def cusp (R t : ℝ) : ℝ := t * (1 + Real.log R - Real.log t)

lemma cusp_pos {R t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) (hR : t ≤ R) : 0 < cusp R t := by
  have hlog := Real.log_le_log ht hR
  dsimp [cusp]
  exact mul_pos ht (by linarith)

lemma cusp_cont {R t : ℝ} (ht : t ≠ 0) : ContinuousAt (cusp R) t := by
  unfold cusp
  fun_prop (disch := assumption)

lemma cusp_deriv {R t : ℝ} (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    HasDerivAt (cusp R) (Real.log R - Real.log t) t := by
  convert (hasDerivAt_id t).mul
    ((hasDerivAt_const t (1 + Real.log R)).sub (Real.hasDerivAt_log ht)) using 1
  dsimp
  field_simp
  ring

lemma cusp_mono (R : ℝ) : MonotoneOn (cusp R) (Ioc 0 R) := by
  apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (f' := fun t ↦ Real.log R - Real.log t)
    (convex_Ioc _ _)
  · intro t ht
    exact (cusp_cont ht.1.ne').continuousWithinAt
  · intro t ht
    exact (cusp_deriv (interior_subset ht).1.ne').hasDerivWithinAt
  · intro t ht
    exact sub_nonneg.mpr (Real.log_le_log (interior_subset ht).1 (interior_subset ht).2)

lemma cusp_le {R t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) (hR : t ≤ R) : cusp R t ≤ R := by
  have h := cusp_mono R ⟨ht, hR⟩ ⟨ht.trans_le hR, le_rfl⟩ hR
  simpa [cusp] using h

lemma cusp_local (F : ℂ → ℂ) (hF : AnalyticAt ℂ F 0) (hF0 : F 0 ≠ 0)
    (R M : ℝ) (hR : ‖F 0‖ ≤ R)
    (hM : ‖deriv F 0‖ = M * cusp R ‖F 0‖)
    (hm : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 (0 : ℂ),
      (1-‖z‖^2) * ‖deriv F z‖ ≤ M * cusp R ‖F z‖) : M ≤ 2 := by
  let q : ℂ → ℂ := fun z ↦ Complex.log (F z / F 0)
  let c : ℝ := 1 + Real.log R - Real.log ‖F 0‖
  have hc : 0 < c := by
    have hlog := Real.log_le_log (norm_pos_iff.mpr hF0) hR
    dsimp [c]
    linarith
  have hsl0 : F 0 / F 0 ∈ Complex.slitPlane := by simp [hF0]
  have hq : AnalyticAt ℂ q 0 := (hF.div analyticAt_const hF0).clog hsl0
  have hq0 : q 0 = 0 := by simp [q]
  have hd : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 (0 : ℂ), deriv q z = deriv F z / F z := by
    filter_upwards [hF.eventually_analyticAt,
      (hF.continuousAt.div_const (F 0)).eventually_mem
        (Complex.isOpen_slitPlane.mem_nhds hsl0),
      hF.continuousAt.eventually_ne hF0] with z hz hsl hn
    have hder := (Complex.hasDerivAt_log hsl).comp z
      (hz.differentiableAt.hasDerivAt.div_const (F 0))
    change HasDerivAt q _ z at hder
    rw [hder.deriv]
    field_simp
  apply halfplane_local q hq hq0 c M hc
  · rw [hd.self_of_nhds, norm_div, hM]
    dsimp [cusp, c]
    field_simp
  · filter_upwards [hm, hd, hF.continuousAt.eventually_ne hF0] with z hm hd hn
    rw [hd, norm_div, ← mul_div_assoc, div_le_iff₀ (norm_pos_iff.mpr hn)]
    have hre : c - (q z).re = 1 + Real.log R - Real.log ‖F z‖ := by
      simp only [q, Complex.log_re, norm_div,
        Real.log_div (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr hn) (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr hF0), c]
      ring
    rw [hre]
    simpa [cusp, mul_assoc, mul_left_comm, mul_comm] using hm

noncomputable def diskShift (b z : ℂ) : ℂ := (b+z)/(1+conj b*z)

@[simp] lemma diskShift_zero (b : ℂ) : diskShift b 0 = b := by simp [diskShift]

lemma diskShift_analytic (b : ℂ) : AnalyticAt ℂ (diskShift b) 0 := by
  apply (analyticAt_const.add analyticAt_id).div
    (analyticAt_const.add (analyticAt_const.mul analyticAt_id))
  simp

lemma diskShift_deriv (b z : ℂ) (hden : 1+conj b*z ≠ 0) :
    HasDerivAt (diskShift b) ((1 - b*conj b)/(1+conj b*z)^2) z := by
  convert ((hasDerivAt_const z b).add (hasDerivAt_id z)).div
    ((hasDerivAt_const z 1).add ((hasDerivAt_id z).const_mul (conj b))) hden using 1
  dsimp
  ring

lemma diskShift_norm_deriv (b z : ℂ) (hb : ‖b‖ < 1) (hden : 1+conj b*z ≠ 0) :
    ‖deriv (diskShift b) z‖ = (1-‖b‖^2)/‖1+conj b*z‖^2 := by
  rw [(diskShift_deriv b z hden).deriv, norm_div, norm_pow, Complex.mul_conj']
  norm_cast
  rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos]
  nlinarith [norm_nonneg b]

lemma diskShift_weight (b z : ℂ) (hb : ‖b‖ < 1) (hden : 1+conj b*z ≠ 0) :
    (1-‖z‖^2)*‖deriv (diskShift b) z‖ = 1-‖diskShift b z‖^2 := by
  rw [diskShift_norm_deriv b z hb hden, diskShift, norm_div, div_pow,
    ← mul_div_assoc, sub_div' (pow_ne_zero 2 (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr hden))]
  congr 1
  simp [Complex.sq_norm, Complex.normSq_apply]
  ring

lemma cusp_local_at (F : ℂ → ℂ) (b : ℂ) (hF : AnalyticAt ℂ F b)
    (hb : ‖b‖ < 1) (hF0 : F b ≠ 0) (R M : ℝ) (hR : ‖F b‖ ≤ R)
    (hM : (1-‖b‖^2)*‖deriv F b‖ = M * cusp R ‖F b‖)
    (hm : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 b,
      (1-‖z‖^2) * ‖deriv F z‖ ≤ M * cusp R ‖F z‖) : M ≤ 2 := by
  let G : ℂ → ℂ := F ∘ diskShift b
  have hG : AnalyticAt ℂ G 0 :=
    (show AnalyticAt ℂ F (diskShift b 0) by simpa using hF).comp (diskShift_analytic b)
  have hden : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 (0 : ℂ), 1+conj b*z ≠ 0 :=
    (continuousAt_const.add (continuousAt_const.mul continuousAt_id)).eventually_ne (by simp)
  have hd : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 (0 : ℂ),
      (1-‖z‖^2)*‖deriv G z‖ =
        (1-‖diskShift b z‖^2)*‖deriv F (diskShift b z)‖ := by
    have hcomp : Tendsto (diskShift b) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 b) := by
      simpa using (diskShift_analytic b).continuousAt.tendsto
    filter_upwards [hden, hcomp.eventually hF.eventually_analyticAt] with z hz hf
    have hder := hf.differentiableAt.hasDerivAt.comp z (diskShift_deriv b z hz)
    change HasDerivAt G _ z at hder
    rw [hder.deriv, norm_mul, ← (diskShift_deriv b z hz).deriv]
    rw [show (1-‖z‖^2)*(‖deriv F (diskShift b z)‖*‖deriv (diskShift b) z‖) =
      ((1-‖z‖^2)*‖deriv (diskShift b) z‖)*‖deriv F (diskShift b z)‖ by ring,
      diskShift_weight b z hb hz]
  apply cusp_local G hG (by simpa [G] using hF0) R M (by simpa [G] using hR)
  · have h := hd.self_of_nhds
    simp only [norm_zero, zero_pow (by norm_num : 2 ≠ 0), sub_zero, one_mul,
      diskShift_zero] at h
    simpa [G, h] using hM
  · have hcomp : Tendsto (diskShift b) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 b) := by
      simpa using (diskShift_analytic b).continuousAt.tendsto
    filter_upwards [hd, hcomp.eventually hm] with z hd hm
    rw [hd]
    exact hm

/-- Landau's derivative estimate for a plane domain containing no disk of radius `R`.
We maximize the pulled-back cusp metric on the closed unit disk. At a maximum, a nearest
point of the complement supplies a smooth supporting metric. -/
lemma landau_deriv_bound (F : ℂ → ℂ) (Ω : Set ℂ) (hΩ : IsOpen Ω)
    (hF : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ F (closedBall 0 1))
    (hmap : MapsTo F (closedBall 0 1) Ω) (R : ℝ)
    (hno : ∀ w : ℂ, ¬ ball w R ⊆ Ω) : ‖deriv F 0‖ ≤ 2*R := by
  have hne : Ωᶜ.Nonempty := by
    obtain ⟨a, ha, hna⟩ := not_subset.mp (hno 0)
    exact ⟨a, hna⟩
  let δ : ℂ → ℝ := fun z ↦ infDist (F z) Ωᶜ
  have hδpos : ∀ z ∈ closedBall (0 : ℂ) 1, 0 < δ z := by
    intro z hz
    exact (hΩ.isClosed_compl.notMem_iff_infDist_pos hne).mp (by simpa using hmap hz)
  have hδlt : ∀ z : ℂ, δ z < R := by
    intro z
    by_contra h
    exact hno (F z) ((ball_subset_ball (le_of_not_gt h)).trans ball_infDist_compl_subset)
  have hcpos : ∀ z ∈ closedBall (0 : ℂ) 1, 0 < cusp R (δ z) :=
    fun z hz ↦ cusp_pos (hδpos z hz) (hδlt z).le
  let m : ℂ → ℝ := fun z ↦ (1-‖z‖^2)*‖deriv F z‖ / cusp R (δ z)
  have hmcont : ContinuousOn m (closedBall 0 1) := by
    apply ContinuousOn.div
      ((continuous_const.sub (continuous_norm.pow 2)).continuousOn.mul hF.deriv.continuousOn.norm)
    · intro z hz
      apply (cusp_cont (hδpos z hz).ne').comp_continuousWithinAt
      exact (continuous_infDist_pt Ωᶜ).continuousAt.comp_continuousWithinAt
        (hF z hz).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · exact fun z hz ↦ (hcpos z hz).ne'
  have hz0 : (0 : ℂ) ∈ closedBall 0 1 := by simp
  by_contra hbound
  have hd0 : 2*R < ‖deriv F 0‖ := lt_of_not_ge hbound
  have hm0 : 2 < m 0 := by
    dsimp [m]
    simp only [norm_zero, zero_pow (by norm_num : 2 ≠ 0), sub_zero, one_mul]
    apply (lt_div_iff₀ (hcpos 0 hz0)).mpr
    have hle := cusp_le (hδpos 0 hz0) (hδlt 0).le
    linarith
  obtain ⟨b, hb, hbmax⟩ := (isCompact_closedBall (0 : ℂ) 1).exists_isMaxOn
    ⟨0, hz0⟩ hmcont
  have hmb : 2 < m b := hm0.trans_le (hbmax hz0)
  have hb1 : ‖b‖ < 1 := by
    have hble : ‖b‖ ≤ 1 := by simpa using hb
    by_contra h
    have he : ‖b‖ = 1 := le_antisymm hble (le_of_not_gt h)
    have hmz : m b = 0 := by simp [m, he]
    linarith
  obtain ⟨a, ha, hda⟩ := hΩ.isClosed_compl.exists_infDist_eq_dist hne (F b)
  have hda : δ b = ‖F b-a‖ := by simpa [δ, dist_eq_norm] using hda
  have hfa : F b-a ≠ 0 := by
    apply norm_ne_zero_iff.mp
    rw [← hda]
    exact (hδpos b hb).ne'
  have hfar : ‖F b-a‖ < R := hda ▸ hδlt b
  have hlocal : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 b,
      (1-‖z‖^2)*‖deriv (fun z ↦ F z-a) z‖ ≤ m b * cusp R ‖F z-a‖ := by
    filter_upwards [isOpen_ball.mem_nhds (show b ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1 by simpa using hb1),
      ((hF b hb).continuousAt.sub_const a).norm.eventually (gt_mem_nhds hfar)]
      with z hz hnorm
    have hzc : z ∈ closedBall (0 : ℂ) 1 := ball_subset_closedBall hz
    have hδle : δ z ≤ ‖F z-a‖ := by
      simpa [δ, dist_eq_norm] using infDist_le_dist_of_mem ha (x := F z)
    have hcle : cusp R (δ z) ≤ cusp R ‖F z-a‖ :=
      cusp_mono R ⟨hδpos z hzc, (hδlt z).le⟩
        ⟨(hδpos z hzc).trans_le hδle, hnorm.le⟩ hδle
    rw [deriv_sub_const]
    have hmax : (1-‖z‖^2)*‖deriv F z‖ ≤ m b * cusp R (δ z) :=
      (div_le_iff₀ (hcpos z hzc)).mp (hbmax hzc)
    exact hmax.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hcle (by linarith))
  have hM : (1-‖b‖^2)*‖deriv (fun z ↦ F z-a) b‖ = m b * cusp R ‖F b-a‖ := by
    rw [deriv_sub_const, ← hda]
    exact (div_mul_cancel₀ _ (hcpos b hb).ne').symm
  have hlast := cusp_local_at (fun z ↦ F z-a) b ((hF b hb).sub analyticAt_const)
    hb1 hfa R (m b) hfar.le hM hlocal
  linarith

lemma landau_disk (f : ℂ → ℂ) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1))
    (hd : deriv f 0 = 1) : ∃ w : ℂ, ball w (49/100 : ℝ) ⊆ f '' ball 0 1 := by
  have hfa := hf.analyticOnNhd isOpen_ball
  have hΩ : IsOpen (f '' ball 0 1) := by
    rcases hfa.is_constant_or_isOpen (convex_ball (0 : ℂ) 1).isPreconnected with hc | ho
    · obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := hc
      have he : f =ᶠ[𝓝 (0 : ℂ)] (fun _ ↦ w) := by
        filter_upwards [ball_mem_nhds (0 : ℂ) (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1)] with z hz
        exact hw z hz
      have hder := he.deriv_eq
      simp [hd] at hder
    · exact ho _ Subset.rfl isOpen_ball
  let F : ℂ → ℂ := fun z ↦ f ((99/100 : ℂ)*z)
  have hscale : ∀ z ∈ closedBall (0 : ℂ) 1, (99/100 : ℂ)*z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1 := by
    intro z hz
    have hz' : ‖z‖ ≤ 1 := by simpa using hz
    simp only [mem_ball, dist_zero_right, norm_mul]
    norm_num
    linarith
  have hF : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ F (closedBall 0 1) := by
    intro z hz
    exact (hfa _ (hscale z hz)).comp (analyticAt_const.mul analyticAt_id)
  have hmap : MapsTo F (closedBall 0 1) (f '' ball 0 1) := by
    intro z hz
    exact ⟨_, hscale z hz, rfl⟩
  have hdF : deriv F 0 = 99/100 := by
    have hder := (hf.differentiableAt
      (ball_mem_nhds (0 : ℂ) (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1))).hasDerivAt
    rw [hd] at hder
    have hder' : HasDerivAt f 1 ((99/100 : ℂ)*0) := by simpa using hder
    have hcomp := hder'.comp 0 ((hasDerivAt_id (0 : ℂ)).const_mul (99/100 : ℂ))
    simpa [F] using hcomp.deriv
  by_contra hno
  push_neg at hno
  have hb := landau_deriv_bound F (f '' ball 0 1) hΩ hF hmap (49/100) hno
  rw [hdF] at hb
  norm_num at hb

/-- Since the definition imposes no openness condition on `S`, a set-theoretic section
of the image suffices for its injectivity requirement. -/
lemma injective_landau_disk (f : ℂ → ℂ) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1))
    (hd : deriv f 0 = 1) :
    ∃ S ⊆ ball 0 1, ∃ x : ℂ, ball x (49/100 : ℝ) ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := landau_disk f hf hd
  obtain ⟨S, hS, hi, he⟩ := (show SurjOn f (ball 0 1) (ball x (49/100 : ℝ)) from hx).exists_subset_injOn_image_eq
  exact ⟨S, hS, x, he.symm.subset, hi⟩

lemma radius_set_bdd : BddAbove {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ,
    DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) → deriv f 0 = 1 →
      ∃ S ⊆ ball 0 1, ∃ x, ball x B ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S} := by
  refine ⟨1, fun B hB ↦ ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨S, hS, x, hx, _⟩ := hB id differentiableOn_id (by simp)
  have hsub : ball x B ⊆ ball (0 : ℂ) 1 := by simpa using hx.trans (image_mono hS)
  by_contra hn
  have hn : 1 < B := lt_of_not_ge hn
  have hp : x + 1 ∈ ball x B := by simpa [mem_ball, dist_eq_norm] using hn
  have hm : x - 1 ∈ ball x B := by simpa [mem_ball, dist_eq_norm] using hn
  have hp' : ‖x+1‖ < 1 := by simpa using hsub hp
  have hm' : ‖x-1‖ < 1 := by simpa using hsub hm
  have htri := norm_sub_le (x+1) (x-1)
  rw [show x+1-(x-1) = 2 by ring] at htri
  norm_num at htri
  linarith

lemma log_gamma_feq {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) :
    (Real.log ∘ Real.Gamma) (y + 1) = (Real.log ∘ Real.Gamma) y + Real.log y := by
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, Real.Gamma_add_one hy.ne',
    Real.log_mul hy.ne' (Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos hy).ne']
  ring

lemma gamma_upper_test (x C : ℝ) (a b n : ℕ)
    (hx : 0 < x) (hx1 : x ≤ 1) (hC : 0 < C) (hb : 0 < b)
    (hab : (b : ℝ) * x = a)
    (ht : ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)^a * (n.factorial : ℝ)^b <
      C^b * (∏ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (x + k))^b) :
    Real.Gamma x < C := by
  have hp : 0 < ∏ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (x + (k : ℝ)) := by
    apply Finset.prod_pos
    intro k hk
    positivity
  have he : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), Real.log (x + (k : ℝ)) =
      Real.log (∏ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (x + (k : ℝ))) := by
    rw [Real.log_prod]
    intro k hk
    positivity
  have h := Real.BohrMollerup.le_logGammaSeq Real.convexOn_log_Gamma
    (@log_gamma_feq) hx hx1 n
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, Real.Gamma_one, Real.log_one, zero_add,
    Real.BohrMollerup.logGammaSeq, he] at h
  have hlog := Real.strictMonoOn_log
    (show 0 < ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)^a * (n.factorial : ℝ)^b by positivity)
    (show 0 < C^b * (∏ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (x + (k : ℝ)))^b by positivity) ht
  rw [Real.log_mul (by positivity) (by positivity),
    Real.log_mul (by positivity) (by positivity), Real.log_pow, Real.log_pow,
    Real.log_pow, Real.log_pow] at hlog
  push_cast at hlog
  by_contra hneg
  have hle : Real.log C ≤ Real.log (Real.Gamma x) :=
    Real.log_le_log hC (le_of_not_gt hneg)
  have hb' : (0 : ℝ) < b := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hb
  rw [← hab] at hlog
  nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hle.trans h) hb'.le]

lemma gamma_lower_test (x C : ℝ) (a b n : ℕ)
    (hx : 0 < x) (hC : 0 < C) (hb : 0 < b) (hn : n ≠ 0)
    (hab : (b : ℝ) * x = a)
    (ht : C^b * (∏ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (x + k))^b <
      (n : ℝ)^a * (n.factorial : ℝ)^b) :
    C < Real.Gamma x := by
  have hp : 0 < ∏ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (x + (k : ℝ)) := by
    apply Finset.prod_pos
    intro k hk
    positivity
  have he : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), Real.log (x + (k : ℝ)) =
      Real.log (∏ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (x + (k : ℝ))) := by
    rw [Real.log_prod]
    intro k hk
    positivity
  have h := Real.BohrMollerup.ge_logGammaSeq Real.convexOn_log_Gamma
    (@log_gamma_feq) hx hn
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, Real.Gamma_one, Real.log_one, zero_add,
    Real.BohrMollerup.logGammaSeq, he] at h
  have hn' : (0 : ℝ) < n := Nat.cast_pos.mpr (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hn)
  have hlog := Real.strictMonoOn_log
    (show 0 < C^b * (∏ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (x + (k : ℝ)))^b by positivity)
    (show 0 < (n : ℝ)^a * (n.factorial : ℝ)^b by positivity) ht
  rw [Real.log_mul (by positivity) (by positivity),
    Real.log_mul (by positivity) (by positivity), Real.log_pow, Real.log_pow,
    Real.log_pow, Real.log_pow] at hlog
  by_contra hneg
  have hle : Real.log (Real.Gamma x) ≤ Real.log C :=
    Real.log_le_log (Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos hx) (le_of_not_gt hneg)
  have hb' : (0 : ℝ) < b := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hb
  rw [← hab] at hlog
  nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (h.trans hle) hb'.le]

set_option maxRecDepth 10000 in
set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
/-- A rational bound, using log-convexity of Gamma and exact finite products. -/
lemma gamma_value_lt :
    Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (11 / 12) /
      (Real.Gamma (1 / 4) * Real.sqrt (1 + Real.sqrt 3)) < 49 / 100 := by
  have h1 : Real.Gamma (1 / 3) < 27 / 10 := by
    apply gamma_upper_test (1 / 3) (27 / 10) 1 3 16 <;>
      norm_num [Finset.prod_range_succ, Nat.factorial]
  have h2 : Real.Gamma (11 / 12) < 107 / 100 := by
    apply gamma_upper_test (11 / 12) (107 / 100) 11 12 8 <;>
      norm_num [Finset.prod_range_succ, Nat.factorial]
  have h3 : 18 / 5 < Real.Gamma (1 / 4) := by
    apply gamma_lower_test (1 / 4) (18 / 5) 1 4 32 <;>
      norm_num [Finset.prod_range_succ, Nat.factorial]
  have hs : (33 / 20 : ℝ) < Real.sqrt (1 + Real.sqrt 3) := by
    have hsq := Real.sq_sqrt (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ 3 by norm_num)
    have hs0 := Real.sqrt_nonneg (3 : ℝ)
    have hs1 := Real.sq_sqrt (show 0 ≤ 1 + Real.sqrt 3 by positivity)
    have hs2 := Real.sqrt_nonneg (1 + Real.sqrt 3)
    have ht : (173 / 100 : ℝ) < Real.sqrt 3 := by nlinarith
    nlinarith
  have hp1 := Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos (show (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 3 by norm_num)
  have hp2 := Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos (show (0 : ℝ) < 11 / 12 by norm_num)
  have hp3 := Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos (show (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 4 by norm_num)
  rw [div_lt_iff₀ (by positivity)]
  have hmul := mul_lt_mul h1 h2.le hp2 (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 27 / 10)
  have hden := mul_lt_mul h3 hs.le (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 33 / 20) hp3.le
  nlinarith

end Aux

/-- The stated equality is false for the definition in this file, which allows
arbitrary subsets `S` rather than open univalence domains. -/
theorem blochConstant_exact_value.disproof :
    ¬ (blochConstant = Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (11 / 12) /
    (Real.Gamma (1 / 4) * Real.sqrt (1 + Real.sqrt 3))) := by
  have hlow : (49 / 100 : ℝ) ≤ blochConstant :=
    le_csSup Aux.radius_set_bdd Aux.injective_landau_disk
  intro h
  rw [h] at hlow
  exact (not_lt_of_ge hlow) Aux.gamma_value_lt

/-- The **Univalent Bloch constant** $B_u$ is the largest radius such that every univalent
holomorphic function on the unit disk with $f'(0) = 1$ has a schlicht disk of that radius in its
image. -/
noncomputable def univalentBlochConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, InjOn f (ball 0 1) → DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) →
    deriv f 0 = 1 → ∃ S ⊆ ball 0 1, ∃ x, ball x B ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S}

/-- The **Landau constant** $L$ is the largest radius such that every holomorphic function on the
unit disk with $f'(0) = 1$ has a disk of that radius contained in its image. -/
noncomputable def landauConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) → deriv f 0 = 1 →
    ∃ x, ball x B ⊆ f '' (ball 0 1)}

end Bloch
```

title: Likely misformalization in `Wikipedia/Bloch.lean`

body:
## Problem

The source asks to characterize the composite integers `n` satisfying `f(n) = n / P(n)`. The current declaration instead places a proposition-valued `answer(sorry)` after `n` and its hypotheses have been bound:

```lean
theorem erdos_700.parts.i (n : ℕ) (hn : ¬ n.Prime) (hn1 : 1 < n) :
    f n = n / P n ↔ answer(sorry)
```

This permits replacing the answer with `f n = n / P n`, making the theorem `P ↔ P` independently for each admissible `n`. It therefore does not require one characterization of all such composite integers. This is a defect in the formal question, not a solution of Erdős Problem 700.

Source: https://www.erdosproblems.com/700

## Proposed fix

State part (a) as one set-level answer:

```lean
theorem erdos_700.parts.i :
    {n : ℕ | ¬ n.Prime ∧ 1 < n ∧ f n = n / P n} = answer(sorry)
```

and add a signature regression test.

I have a local patch with a kernel-checked self-answer reproduction, changed-scope build, test-driver validation, and no new proof/axiom bypass. I plan to submit it in a focused PR.
title: Erdős 700(a): answer is scoped per n rather than over the characterization

body:
### Describe the misformalization
In `erdos_394.variants.lower_bound` the two sides of `≫` are swapped relative to the docstring.

Because of this, the file's open `hall_conjecture` would follow from this `research solved` statement (see below).

https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/f40ecd9b3b79a7aa1a64b7d2f3b2623d4a6c3081/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/394.lean#L106-L113

The docstring says the sum dominates (a trivial **lower** bound):

> Since $t_2(p)=p-1$ for prime $p$ it is trivial that $\sum_{n\leq x}t_2(n)\gg \frac{x^2}{\log x}$.

but the code puts the sum on the other side:

```lean
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_394.variants.lower_bound :
    (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 / Real.log x) ≫
    (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊, (t 2 n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry
```

[`f ≫ g` is notation for `g =O[atTop] f`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/33c6a2dcafc5e3cdebfc083203b0a051309ea5b4/FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/Basic.lean#L24-L25).

So as written this states the **upper** bound $\sum_{n\le x} t_2(n) = O(x^2/\log x)$ — the reverse of the docstring — while being marked `research solved`.

### Trivial proof/disproof
The swap is visible by comparing the docstring with the code above.

And since $\log 2 < 1$, an $O(x^2/\log x)$ upper bound implies $o(x^2/(\log x)^c)$ for every $c < \log 2$ — which is exactly the statement of the open `hall_conjecture`.

### Suggested fix
Swap the arguments back:

```lean
theorem erdos_394.variants.lower_bound :
    (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊, (t 2 n : ℝ)) ≫
    (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 / Real.log x) := by
  sorry
```

No `@[category ...]` annotation needs to change:

- `lower_bound` stays `research solved` — after the swap it is the trivial known lower bound described in the docstring.
- `hall_conjecture` stays `research open` — the fix is what makes that label meaningful again (currently it could be "closed" as a corollary of a `research solved` statement, without any mathematics).
- No other declaration in the file is affected.

### Additional context
This is only a statement correction — the Erdős–Hall conjecture (`hall_conjecture`) itself remains open. Related status-sync issue: #4803.

- [ ] I plan on working on this issue
- [x] This issue is up for grabs: I would like to see this misformalization fixed by somebody else

### Issue

`FormalConjectures/OEIS/211417.lean`'s `general_divisibility` asserts

```lean
∃ D : ℤ, ∀ n : ℕ, (divisorProduct n r) ∣ (D * (a n : ℤ))
```

Since every integer divides `0`, the witness `D = 0` satisfies this for every `r` — the statement as written is vacuous (3-line proof):

```lean
theorem general_divisibility_is_vacuous (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) :
    ∃ D : ℤ, ∀ n : ℕ, (divisorProduct n r) ∣ (D * (a n : ℤ)) :=
  ⟨0, fun n => by simp⟩
```

### Suggested fix

Strengthen to `∃ D : ℤ, 0 < D ∧ ∀ n, divisorProduct n r ∣ D * a n` (this matches Bala's intent on the OEIS page).

### Note

PR #5023 proves the strengthened form (and the original one via the same positive witness), so accepting that PR resolves both the conjecture and this statement issue; filing separately so the statement defect is tracked even if the PR is handled independently.

body:
### Describe the misformalization

`FormalConjectures/OEIS/100434.lean` defines
```lean
def b (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  if n % 2 = 0 then c (n + 1)
  else c (n - 1)
```
and records Dement's three conjectured identities `c n + d n = b n`,
`e n + f n = b n`, `g n + a n = b n` as `research open`.

As written, all three are refutable at `n = 0` (by `decide`-level
computation): `c 0 + d 0 = 1 + 2 = 3` while `b 0 = c 1 = -3`.

This appears to be a transcription of a sign-sloppy OEIS comment taken
literally. Dement's comment describes `c` as "A001333, apart from signs"
throughout, and states the identities' meaning as: the sequences
(c+d) = (e+f) = (g+a) "all represent the sequence c with even- and
odd-indexed terms reversed". The intended `b` (matching that description,
the numerics, and the file's own proven lemma `a_even : a (2n) = -c (2n+1)`)
has a minus sign on the even branch:
```lean
def b (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  if n % 2 = 0 then - c (n + 1)
  else c (n - 1)
```
With this corrected `b`, all three identities hold (verified numerically
for n < 2000, and proven — see below).

Related: PR #4560 ("Add OEIS A100434 disproof", closed) disproved the
literal reading; this issue proposes fixing the definition to the intended
statement instead, for which a full proof exists.

### Trivial proof/disproof

Refutation of the current statement at n = 0: `c 0 + d 0 = 3 ≠ -3 = b 0`
(both sides compute by `rfl`/`decide`).

### Suggested fix

Change `b`'s even branch to `- c (n + 1)` (as above), and — if desired —
reclassify the three theorems, since the corrected identities are provable
by `Nat.twoStepInduction` (all six sequences satisfy the same order-4
recurrence `x(n+4) = -6x(n+2) - x(n)`; the divisions in `e`/`f` are
discharged by parity lemmas `2 ∣ d(2k)`, `2 ∣ d(2k+1)`).

We have a complete, sorry-free Lean 4 proof of the three corrected
identities against current mathlib (axioms: propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound only), which we are happy to contribute as a PR if the proposed
fix is acceptable.

### Additional context

Found during a systematic verification pass over the OEIS folder. This
report was prepared with AI assistance (Claude); the refutation and the
corrected-identity proofs are machine-checked.

- [x] I plan on working on this issue (can submit the fix + proofs as a PR)
- [ ] This issue is up for grabs

body:
### Describe the misformalization

`FormalConjectures/OEIS/109074.lean` formalizes the OEIS A109074 conjecture
"binomial(6n-2,2n) / (2*binomial(4n-1,2n)) = A005156(n+1)/A005156(n)".

Two independent problems:

1. **Wrong sequence.** The file defines
   ```lean
   def b (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
     let num : ℕ := (3 * n).choose n
     let den : ℕ := 2 * n + 1
     num / den
   ```
   This is `C(3n, n)/(2n+1)`, i.e. OEIS **A001764** (ternary trees:
   1, 1, 3, 12, 55, 273, ...), not **A005156** (vertically symmetric
   alternating sign matrices: 1, 1, 3, 26, 646, 45885, ...). The two agree
   up to n = 2 and diverge at n = 3 (12 vs 26).

2. **Wrong shift.** Even with the correct A005156, the relation matching
   the numerics is `frac n = A005156(n) / A005156(n-1)`, not
   `A005156(n+1) / A005156(n)`:
   frac 2 = 3 = A(2)/A(1), frac 3 = 26/3 = A(3)/A(2), frac 4 = 323/13 = A(4)/A(3).

### Trivial proof/disproof

The formalized statement is refutable at `n = 1` by computation:
`frac 1 = C(4,2) / (2 * C(3,2)) = 6/6 = 1`, while
`b 2 / b 1 = (C(6,2)/5) / (C(3,1)/3) = 3 / 1 = 3`, and `1 ≠ 3`.
(A `decide`/`norm_num` disproof of the ∀-statement's `n = 1` instance goes
through directly on the file's definitions.)

### Suggested fix

Define A005156 by the Robbins–Kuperberg product formula (proved by
Kuperberg, so a valid closed form for the entry), e.g.
`A005156 n = ∏ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, ((6k-2)! * (2k-1)!) / ((4k-1)! * (4k-2)!)`
(with the standard 1/2^k normalization folded in as in the OEIS Maple
code), and state the conjecture as
`frac n = A005156 n / A005156 (n-1)` for `n ≥ 1`.

Remark: with the product-formula definition the corrected statement reduces
to a finite factorial identity
`frac n = (6n-2)! (2n-1)! / (2 * (4n-1)! (4n-2)!)`,
so the mathematical content of the OEIS conjecture is precisely Kuperberg's
theorem; the entry may deserve a category other than `research open` after
the fix.

### Additional context

Found during a systematic verification pass over the OEIS folder. All
numerical claims above were checked with exact rational arithmetic. This
report was prepared with AI assistance (Claude); the refutation at n = 1 is
machine-checked.

### Choose either option

- [x] This issue is up for grabs: I would like to see this misformalization fixed by somebody else

### Describe the misformalization

`VCDimConvex.exists_hasAddVCNDimAtMost_n_of_convex_rn_add_one` is quantified over all `n : ℕ`, including `n = 0`, where it is false for degenerate reasons (`Fin 0 → Fin (d + 1)` is a singleton, so translates of `{0} ⊆ ℝ¹` realize every pattern and no `d` works). This is presumably not the intended statement.

Permalink: https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/9943b0a06a1c311a68c31193460896694f77bd7a/FormalConjectures/Other/VCDimConvex.lean#L60-L64


### Trivial proof/disproof

Compiles against current main (`9943b0a`, Lean 4.27.0); `#print axioms`: `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

```lean
import FormalConjectures.Other.VCDimConvex

open scoped EuclideanGeometry Pointwise

namespace VCDimConvex

theorem exists_hasAddVCNDimAtMost_n_of_convex_rn_add_one_n0_false :
    ¬ (∃ d : ℕ, ∀ C : Set (Fin (0 + 1) → ℝ),
      Convex ℝ C → HasAddVCNDimAtMost C 0 d) := by
  classical
  rintro ⟨d, hd⟩
  let C : Set (Fin 1 → ℝ) := {0}
  have hC : Convex ℝ C := convex_singleton 0
  have h := hd C hC
  unfold HasAddVCNDimAtMost at h
  let i₀ : Fin 0 → Fin (d + 1) := fun i => Fin.elim0 i
  let x : Fin 0 → Fin (d + 1) → (Fin 1 → ℝ) := fun i => Fin.elim0 i
  let y : Set (Fin 0 → Fin (d + 1)) → (Fin 1 → ℝ) :=
    fun s => if i₀ ∈ s then 0 else 1
  apply h x y
  intro i s
  have hi : i = i₀ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  subst i
  simp [C, x, y]

#print axioms exists_hasAddVCNDimAtMost_n_of_convex_rn_add_one_n0_false

end VCDimConvex
```

body:
### Describe the misformalization

[`infinite_isWallSunSunPrime_of_disc_eq`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/WallSunSun.lean#L154-L158) is marked `research open`:

```lean
theorem infinite_isWallSunSunPrime_of_disc_eq {D : ℤ}
    (hD : IsFundamentalDiscr D) (hD₁ : D ≠ 1) :
    {p : ℕ | ∃ a b, a ^ 2 - 4 * b = D ∧
      IsLucasWieferichPrime a b p}.Infinite := by
  sorry
```

The source says that, for every non-one fundamental discriminant `D`, there are infinitely many Wall–Sun–Sun primes with discriminant `D`. The current Lean statement interprets

```text
p is a Wall–Sun–Sun prime with discriminant D
```

as the existence of some Lucas parameters `(a,b)` with `a² - 4b = D`. Because this existential quantifier is inside the predicate on `p`, a different pair may be chosen for every prime.

This is a possible literal reading of the source, but it is not clear that it is the intended one.

### Trivial proof/disproof
Every odd prime `p` not dividing `D` belongs to the formalized set. Choose

```text
a = p²    if D ≡ 1 (mod 4),
a = 2p²   if 4 ∣ D,
b = (a² - D) / 4.
```

Then `a² - 4b = D` and `p² ∣ a`. Since `p ∤ D`, the Jacobi symbol `J(D | p)` is `±1`, so `n = p - J(D | p)` is positive and even. The recurrence

```text
U₀ = 0,  U₁ = 1,  Uₙ₊₂ = a Uₙ₊₁ - b Uₙ
```

implies `a ∣ U₂ₖ(a,b)`. Hence `p² ∣ Uₙ(a,b)`, proving `IsLucasWieferichPrime a b p`. Only finitely many odd primes divide `D`, so the current set is infinite.

<details>
 <summary>Lean Proof</summary>

The following compiles against the current Formal Conjectures environment. 
```lean
import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.WallSunSun

open NumberField
open scoped NumberTheorySymbols

theorem wallSunSunCurrentFormalizationSolved {D : ℤ}
    (hD : IsFundamentalDiscr D) (hD₁ : D ≠ 1) :
    {p : ℕ | ∃ a b, a ^ 2 - 4 * b = D ∧ IsLucasWieferichPrime a b p}.Infinite := by
  have hD₀ : D ≠ 0 := by
    rintro rfl
    simp [IsFundamentalDiscr] at hD
  rw [Set.infinite_iff_exists_gt]
  intro N
  obtain ⟨p, hp_bound, hp⟩ :=
    Nat.exists_infinite_primes (max (N + 1) (max 3 (D.natAbs + 1)))
  have hpN : N < p := by omega
  have hpD : D.natAbs < p := by omega
  have hp_two : p ≠ 2 := by omega
  have hp_odd : Odd p := hp.odd_of_ne_two hp_two
  have hp_not_dvd_natAbs : ¬p ∣ D.natAbs := by
    intro h
    have := Nat.le_of_dvd (Int.natAbs_pos.mpr hD₀) h
    omega
  have hp_not_dvd : ¬(p : ℤ) ∣ D := by
    simpa only [Int.natCast_dvd] using hp_not_dvd_natAbs
  have hcop : D.gcd (p : ℤ) = 1 := by
    rw [Int.gcd_eq_natAbs, Int.natAbs_natCast, Nat.gcd_comm]
    exact hp.coprime_iff_not_dvd.mpr hp_not_dvd_natAbs
  have hJ : J(D | p) = 1 ∨ J(D | p) = -1 := jacobiSym.eq_one_or_neg_one hcop
  have hU_even (a b : ℤ) (ha : ((p ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ a) (k : ℕ) :
      ((p ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ LucasSequence.U a b (2 * k) := by
    induction k with
    | zero => simp [LucasSequence.U]
    | succ k ih =>
        rw [show 2 * (k + 1) = 2 * k + 2 by omega, LucasSequence.U]
        exact (ha.mul_right _).sub (ih.mul_left _)
  have mkLWP (a b : ℤ) (hab : a ^ 2 - 4 * b = D)
      (ha : ((p ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ a) : IsLucasWieferichPrime a b p := by
    refine ⟨hp, hp_odd, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rwa [hab]
    · apply Int.modEq_zero_iff_dvd.mpr
      obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hp_odd
      rcases hJ with hJ | hJ
      · have hidx : ((p : ℤ) - 1).toNat = 2 * k := by
          rw [hk]
          norm_num
          change (((2 * k : ℕ) : ℤ)).toNat = 2 * k
          exact Int.toNat_natCast _
        rw [hab, hJ, hidx]
        exact hU_even a b ha k
      · have hidx : ((p : ℤ) - (-1)).toNat = 2 * (k + 1) := by
          rw [hk]
          norm_num
          omega
        rw [hab, hJ, hidx]
        exact hU_even a b ha (k + 1)
  refine ⟨p, ?_, hpN⟩
  change ∃ a b, a ^ 2 - 4 * b = D ∧ IsLucasWieferichPrime a b p
  rcases hD with ⟨⟨d, hd⟩, _, _⟩ | ⟨_, hDmod, _⟩
  · subst D
    refine ⟨2 * ((p ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℤ), ((p ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) ^ 2 - d,
      ?_, mkLWP _ _ ?_ ?_⟩
    · ring
    · ring
    · exact (dvd_refl ((p ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℤ)).mul_left 2
  · obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := hDmod.dvd
    have hD_eq : D = 1 - 4 * d := by omega
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hp_odd
    refine ⟨((p ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℤ),
      4 * (k : ℤ) ^ 4 + 8 * (k : ℤ) ^ 3 + 6 * (k : ℤ) ^ 2 + 2 * k + d,
      ?_, mkLWP _ _ ?_ ?_⟩
    · norm_num [hk, hD_eq]
      ring
    · norm_num [hk, hD_eq]
      ring
    · exact dvd_refl _
```

</details>

### Suggested fix

The current formal statement has an elementary proof, so it should not remain an unproved `research open` declaration in its present form. I suggest:

1. replacing its `sorry` with the formal proof and marking the current statement `research solved`; and
2. documenting explicitly that the proof uses Lucas parameters `(a,b)` that may depend on `p`.

The maintainers should then review whether this interpretation faithfully represents the source:

- If “with discriminant `D`” permits `(a,b)` to vary with `p`, the current statement is correctly formalized and solved.
- If it refers to one fixed Lucas sequence, the statement should instead be reformulated and may remain open.


### Additional context
- [Current Wikipedia definition and conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall%E2%80%93Sun%E2%80%93Sun_prime#Wall%E2%80%93Sun%E2%80%93Sun_primes_with_discriminant_D)
- [Wikipedia edit introducing the infinitude sentence](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?diff=676076025&oldid=676075891)
- [Wikipedia discussion explicitly asking whether `(P,Q)` is fixed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Wall%E2%80%93Sun%E2%80%93Sun_prime#Conjecture_about_discriminants)

### Choose either option

title: Wikipedia/WallSunSun: infinite_isWallSunSunPrime_of_disc_eq is elementary because its Lucas parameters vary with p

body:
## Summary

`Paper/LatinSquare.lean` opens with `variable {n : ℕ}` at line 33. Two `research open`
declarations use `n` in their statements but not in their own binder lists, so each elaborates
as `∀ {n : ℕ}, answer(sorry) ↔ P n` with a **single** answer slot outside the `∀ n`. The
consequence is that `answer(False)` is unreachable in one case and, in the other, the
declaration is provable only if `P n` has the same truth value for every `n` — neither of which
is the intended reading of the `answer(sorry) ↔ …` idiom.

The repository's `AnswerLinter` exists to catch exactly this ("Move the quantifiers outward…"),
but its `contains_early_args` helper reads `decl[2][0]`, the binder list in the theorem's own
`declSig`, and `variable`-introduced binders are not there. I include a machine-checked
demonstration of the blind spot below, since it is probably the more useful half of this report.

https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/Paper/LatinSquare.lean#L33

```lean
variable {n : ℕ}
```

https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/Paper/LatinSquare.lean#L53-L60

```lean
/-- Conjecture 3.2 in [Wa2011]: Each Latin square of odd order has at least one transversal. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem oddOrderLatinSquareTransversal : answer(sorry) ↔
    Odd n → ∀ (L : LatinSquare n), ∃ σ, IsTransversal L σ := by
  sorry
```

https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/Paper/LatinSquare.lean#L84-L91

```lean
/-- Conjecture 5.1 in [Wa2011]: Every latin square has a near-transversal -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem latinSquareNearTransversal : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (L : LatinSquare n), ∃ ρ σ, IsNearTransversal L ρ σ := by
  sorry
```

## Consequences

**`oddOrderLatinSquareTransversal`: `answer(False)` is unreachable.** The right-hand side is
`Odd n → …`, which is *vacuously true* whenever `n` is even. So the answer is forced to `True`
whatever the status of Conjecture 3.2, and the declaration then asserts the conjecture outright
rather than asking it:

```lean
theorem answer_forced_true {Q : ℕ → Prop} (A : Prop) (h : ∀ n : ℕ, A ↔ (Odd n → Q n)) : A :=
  (h 2).mpr (fun h2 => absurd h2 (by decide))
```

The `answer(sorry) ↔ …` idiom exists so that a solver can record either verdict; here one
verdict cannot be recorded.

**`latinSquareNearTransversal`: provable only if the conjecture is `n`-uniform.** Same scoping,
without the vacuity: `∀ {n}, A ↔ P n` says every `P n` has the truth value `A`. If the
near-transversal conjecture held for some orders and failed for others, **no** answer would make
the declaration provable.

The sibling `latinSquareOrder11Transversal` is immune — it fixes `LatinSquare 11`, so `n` never
enters — and is not part of this report.

## The linter blind spot

Machine-checked against Mathlib v4.27.0 (`lean -DautoImplicit=false
-DrelaxedAutoImplicit=false`, exit 0):

```lean
set_option linter.style.answer_attribute true

/-- Explicit binder in the `declSig`: the linter fires. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem explicitBinder (m : ℕ) : answer(sorry) ↔ (0 < m) := by sorry

section
variable {n : ℕ}

/-- Same statement, binder introduced by `variable`: the linter is silent. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem sectionBinder : answer(sorry) ↔ (0 < n) := by sorry

end
```

Output — one warning, on `explicitBinder` only:

```
P7.lean:6:0: warning: Move the quantifiers outward:
instead of
`theorem foo (bar : ℕ) (baz : ℕ) : answer(sorry) ↔ ...`
likely the intention was
`theorem foo : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (bar : ℕ) (baz : ℕ), ...`
```

Nothing is reported for `sectionBinder`, which is the shape both `LatinSquare` declarations
have. Extending `contains_early_args` to consult the elaborated declaration's telescope (or the
section variables in scope) rather than the surface `declSig` binders would close this; that
would fall under #1407.

## Suggested fix

Move the quantifier inside, as the linter's own message says:

```lean
theorem oddOrderLatinSquareTransversal : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n : ℕ, Odd n → ∀ (L : LatinSquare n), ∃ σ, IsTransversal L σ := by
  sorry

theorem latinSquareNearTransversal : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ (L : LatinSquare n), ∃ ρ σ, IsNearTransversal L ρ σ := by
  sorry
```

I have not opened a PR: #4965 is open against this file and would conflict, and whoever lands
first can reasonably carry this change.

## What is *not* claimed

Conjectures 3.2 and 5.1 of [Wa2011] are untouched; both remain open. `molsExistenceProblem`
(line 212) is closable by `rfl` with the set on its right-hand side, but that is the case
CONTRIBUTING explicitly places out of scope ("one can provide trivial answers that aren't
mathematically interesting…"), so I do not report it.

## Duplicate check

Offline sweep of all 1747 issues and 3237 PRs (with per-PR file lists) on `LatinSquare`,
`molsExistenceProblem`, `MOLS`, `Transversal`, and the path
`FormalConjectures/Paper/LatinSquare.lean`. The open PR **#4965** touches this file but changes
only `oddOrderLeq9LatinSquareTransversal` (`answer(sorry)` → `answer(True)`, a `research solved`
declaration), not either declaration reported here — I re-checked its diff immediately before
filing. Issues #2270/#2271/#2272 are the original formalization requests. Not in #4896, #4923 or
#4927.

## Related

Same defect family as #5005 (five instances in `GreensOpenProblems`) and #5008
(`Paper/VoronovskajaTypeFormula`); this one is distinguished by being invisible to the linter
that was written for it.

## Relationship to the C₅[K₄] campaign

Found while auditing `research open` declarations in the non-Wikipedia collections:

https://github.com/Kuberwastaken/c5-k4/blob/aa598efc894f2ab9628ccd8019b41318f20111ac/results/expansion/live-search-2026-08-15/other-corpora-scan.md

## AI assistance disclosure

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic) for the audit, the Lean witnesses and drafting.
The submitter reviewed the declarations, the probe output, and the suggested repair, and takes
responsibility for the submission.

### Choose either option
- [ ] I plan on working on this issue
- [x] This issue is up for grabs: I would like to see this misformalization fixed by somebody else
title: Paper/LatinSquare: two `answer( )` slots sit outside a `variable {n}` binder — `answer(False)` is unreachable, and the AnswerLinter cannot see it

body:
## Summary

`voronovskaja_theorem.bezier_bernstein_operators` puts its `answer( )` slot **inside** the
binders `α`, `f` and `x`, so a closed answer is one real number that must be the limit for every
admissible `α`, `f` and `x`. The constant function is admissible, and on it the Bézier–Bernstein
weights telescope so the sequence is identically `0`. By uniqueness of limits the answer is
therefore **forced to `0`** — at which point the declaration asserts that
`√n (B_{n,α} f(x) − f(x)) → 0` for *every* `C²` function, contradicting the file's own "Known
Results" note and the answer both open PRs on this file propose.

https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/Paper/VoronovskajaTypeFormula.lean#L119-L132

```lean
@[category research open, AMS 26 40 47]
theorem voronovskaja_theorem.bezier_bernstein_operators
    (α : ℝ) (hα_pos : 0 < α) (hα : α ≠ 1)
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) (hx : x ∈ I)
    (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 f I) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.sqrt n * (bezierBernstein n α f x - f x)) atTop
      (𝓝 answer(sorry)) := by
  sorry
```

The file's own statement of the problem is *"determine an explicit expression for it in terms of
`f`, `x`, and `α`"* — precisely the dependence the slot cannot express.

## Proof that the answer is forced to `0`

For constant `f ≡ c`,

```
B_{n,α} f(x) = c · Σ_{k=0}^{n} (J_{n,k}(x)^α − J_{n,k+1}(x)^α) = c · (J_{n,0}(x)^α − J_{n,n+1}(x)^α)
```

by telescoping, and `J_{n,0} = 1` (binomial theorem) while `J_{n,n+1} = 0` (the index set
`Finset.Icc (n+1) n` is empty), so with `α > 0` the bracket is `1 − 0 = 1` and
`B_{n,α} f(x) = c`. The scaled difference is then identically `0`.

Machine-checked with the file's definitions copied verbatim from `main` @ `638da20e`
(`lean -DautoImplicit=false -DrelaxedAutoImplicit=false -DwarningAsError=true`, Mathlib
v4.27.0, exit 0, no `sorry`):

```lean
noncomputable def bernsteinTail (n k : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ :=
  ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc k n, bernsteinPolynomial ℝ n j

noncomputable def bezierBernstein (n : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
    f (k / n) * ((bernsteinTail n k).eval x ^ α - (bernsteinTail n (k + 1)).eval x ^ α)

theorem bernsteinTail_zero (n : ℕ) : bernsteinTail n 0 = 1 := by
  rw [bernsteinTail, ← Nat.range_succ_eq_Icc_zero]
  exact bernsteinPolynomial.sum ℝ n

theorem bernsteinTail_succ_self (n : ℕ) : bernsteinTail n (n + 1) = 0 := by
  simp [bernsteinTail]

theorem bezierBernstein_const (n : ℕ) (α c x : ℝ) (hα : α ≠ 0) :
    bezierBernstein n α (fun _ ↦ c) x = c := by
  rw [bezierBernstein, ← Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_range_sub']
  rw [bernsteinTail_zero, bernsteinTail_succ_self]
  simp [hα]

/-- Any closed `L : ℝ` satisfying the upstream statement for all admissible `α`, `f`, `x`
is `0`. -/
theorem answer_forced_zero (L : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ (α : ℝ), 0 < α → α ≠ 1 → ∀ (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ), x ∈ I → ContDiffOn ℝ 2 f I →
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.sqrt n * (bezierBernstein n α f x - f x)) atTop (𝓝 L)) :
    L = 0 := by
  have hx : (0 : ℝ) ∈ I := ⟨le_refl 0, zero_le_one⟩
  have hf : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 (fun _ : ℝ ↦ (0 : ℝ)) I := contDiffOn_const
  have key := h 2 two_pos (by norm_num) (fun _ ↦ (0 : ℝ)) 0 hx hf
  have hzero : (fun n : ℕ => Real.sqrt n * (bezierBernstein n 2 (fun _ : ℝ ↦ (0 : ℝ)) 0 - 0))
      = fun _ : ℕ => (0 : ℝ) := by
    funext n
    rw [bezierBernstein_const n 2 0 0 two_ne_zero]
    ring
  rw [hzero] at key
  exact (tendsto_nhds_unique tendsto_const_nhds key).symm
```

(`bezierBernstein_const` is also proved, independently, in #4432 — its lemma of the same name.)

## Why `answer := 0` then makes the declaration false

With `L = 0` the declaration says the limit is `0` for **every** `C²` `f`, every `x ∈ [0,1]` and
every `α > 0`, `α ≠ 1`. That contradicts:

* the file's own **Known Results** section — *"Numerical experiments indicate that for
  `α ≠ 1` the quantity `√n (B_{n,α} f(x) − f(x))` may converge to a **non-zero** limit"*;
* the answer proposed in **#4646**, `μ(α)·√(x(1−x))·f′(x)` with
  `μ(α) = ∫₀^∞ ((1−Φ(t))^α − (1−Φ(t)^α)) dt`, which is non-zero for e.g. `f = id`, `x = 1/2`,
  `α ≠ 1`;
* the answer proposed in **#4432**, which is likewise a formula in `α`, `f` and `x`.

So the declaration is either false (if a closed answer is required, as in `with_auxiliary` mode,
where the answer becomes the top-level definition `<decl>._answer`) or answerable only by
capturing the binders, i.e. trivially. Either way it does not ask the source's question.

**This is load-bearing for the two open PRs on this file.** #4646 marks the declaration
`research solved` and attaches a formal proof of the `μ(α)√(x(1−x))f′(x)` formula, but leaves
`answer(sorry)` in place — and that formula cannot be written into the slot as it stands, since
it mentions `α`, `f` and `x`. #4432 records the same formula in the docstring for the same
reason. Fixing the scoping first would let either PR say what it means. I am not disputing the
mathematics in either PR; the point is only that the current statement shape cannot hold their
answer.

## The same scoping recurs twice more in the file

* `voronovskaja_theorem.bezier_bernstein_operators.variants.eventually_smooth` binds
  `let limitFormula : (ℝ → ℝ) → ℝ → ℝ := answer(sorry)` under `(α : ℝ)`, so the formula cannot
  depend on `α` — while `μ(α)` does.
* `...variants.answer_smoothness` binds `let p : ℕ × ((ℝ → ℝ) → ℝ → ℝ) := answer(sorry)` under
  `(α : ℝ)`, likewise.
* `...variants.eventually_smooth.limit_exists` is **correctly** formed: it uses `∃ L` *inside*
  all the binders. It is not part of this report.

## Suggested fix

Make the answer a function of the quantities the source says it depends on:

```lean
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.sqrt n * (bezierBernstein n α f x - f x)) atTop
      (𝓝 ((answer(sorry) : ℝ → (ℝ → ℝ) → ℝ → ℝ) α f x))
```

and correspondingly `(answer(sorry) : ℝ → (ℝ → ℝ) → ℝ → ℝ) α` for `variants.eventually_smooth`,
`(answer(sorry) : ℝ → ℕ × ((ℝ → ℝ) → ℝ → ℝ)) α` for `variants.answer_smoothness`. The idiom is
already used correctly elsewhere in the corpus — `OpenQuantumProblems/13.lean` writes
`IsMaxMUBCount d ((answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℕ) d)`.

I have not opened a PR for this one because #4646 and #4432 are both open against the same
declaration and either would conflict; whoever lands first should probably carry the scoping
change.

## Relation to the repository's own tooling

The `AnswerLinter` message names exactly this defect — *"Move the quantifiers outward … likely
the intention was `theorem foo : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (bar : ℕ) …"* — but its
`stars_with_answer_sorry_iff` check fires only on statements of the form `answer(sorry) ↔ …`,
and this one has a different shape. Compare #33, #1407, and #5005, which reports five instances
of the same defect in `GreensOpenProblems`.

## What is *not* claimed

Abel's problem is untouched: whether the limit exists for `α ≠ 1`, and what it is, is exactly as
open as before. This is a report about what the Lean declaration asserts.

## Duplicate check

Offline sweep of all 1747 issues and 3237 PRs (with per-PR file lists), matched on
`Voronovskaja`, `bezier`, `bernstein`, `VoronovskajaTypeFormula` and the path
`FormalConjectures/Paper/VoronovskajaTypeFormula.lean`. Hits: #1396 (the original formalization
request), #1444 (the implementing PR), #4526 (LaTeX), #4034/#4042 (chores), #4525 (closed), and
the two open PRs #4646 and #4432 discussed above. None reports the scoping defect. Not in
#4896, #4923 or #4927.

## Relationship to the C₅[K₄] campaign

Found while auditing `research open` declarations in the non-Wikipedia collections:

https://github.com/Kuberwastaken/c5-k4/blob/aa598efc894f2ab9628ccd8019b41318f20111ac/results/expansion/live-search-2026-08-15/other-corpora-scan.md

## AI assistance disclosure

The submitter reviewed the declaration, the proof, and the suggested repair, and takes
responsibility for the submission.

title: Paper/VoronovskajaTypeFormula: the `answer` slot in `bezier_bernstein_operators` is scoped under `α`, `f`, `x`, so the constant function forces it to 0

body:
## Summary

Six `research open` declarations in `GreensOpenProblems` put an `answer( )` slot in a position
where the value it must take **depends on a quantifier that encloses the slot**. Each one is
therefore either

* **false**, if the answer is required to be a closed term — which is what `answer( )` means in
  `with_auxiliary` mode, where it becomes the top-level definition `<decl>._answer`; or
* **trivial**, if the answer may capture the enclosing binder, since then it can be the target
  expression itself.

In neither reading does the declaration ask Green's question. Four of the five in Part A come
with a machine-checked disproof of the closed-answer reading, reproduced in full below.

This is the defect the repository's own `AnswerLinter` describes — *"Move the quantifiers
outward … likely the intention was `theorem foo : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (bar : ℕ) …"* — but its
`stars_with_answer_sorry_iff` check only inspects statements of the form
`answer(sorry) ↔ …`, and none of these has that shape, so it never fires. Related: #33, #1407,
#4923.

**Not reported here.** `green_25`, `green_51` and `green_27.equivalent` *are* closable by `rfl` /
`IsEquivalent.refl` with genuinely closed answers, but that is the case CONTRIBUTING explicitly
places out of scope ("one can provide trivial answers that aren't mathematically interesting,
e.g. the set `{n : ℕ | P n}` itself … outside of the scope of this repository"), and #33 already
tracks it as a design question. The items below are different: no answer, trivial or otherwise,
makes them true.

The underlying mathematics is untouched throughout. Every one of Green's questions is exactly as
open as before; these are statements about what the Lean declarations assert.

**Machine-checking method.** No `lake build` was available on this machine (insufficient disk for
the full build; only the `FormalConjecturesUtil` / `FormalConjecturesForMathlib` oleans were
present). Each proof below was checked by copying the relevant definitions **verbatim** from
`main` @ `638da20e` into a standalone file importing `FormalConjecturesUtil`, and running

```
lean -DautoImplicit=false -DrelaxedAutoImplicit=false -DwarningAsError=true probe.lean
```

against Mathlib v4.27.0 — exit code 0, no `sorry`, no errors, no warnings. That checks the
mathematics against the real definitions; it does not check that the files themselves still
build, since I did not build them.

---

# Part A — five slots no closed term can fill

- [ ] **`green_24`** — https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/GreensOpenProblems/24.lean#L52-L54

  ```lean
  theorem green_24 : ∀ n, max013AffineTranslates n = answer(sorry) := by sorry
  ```

  The slot has type `ℕ` and sits under `∀ n`, so a closed answer asserts that
  `max013AffineTranslates` is **constant**. It is not: `max013AffineTranslates 0 = 0` (the only
  `A : Finset ℤ` with `A.card = 0` is `∅`), while `A = {0, 1, 3}` already contributes the pair
  `(0, 1)` — `0 + 3·(1 − 0) = 3 ∈ A` — so `1 ≤ max013AffineTranslates 3`.

  ```lean
  theorem max013_zero : max013AffineTranslates 0 = 0 := by
    have h : { k | ∃ A : Finset ℤ, A.card = 0 ∧
        k = ((A ×ˢ A).filter (fun (x, y) ↦ x ≠ y ∧ x + 3 * (y - x) ∈ A)).card } = {0} := by
      ext k
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨A, hA, rfl⟩
        rw [Finset.card_eq_zero.mp hA]
        simp
      · rintro rfl
        exact ⟨∅, by simp, by simp⟩
    rw [max013AffineTranslates, h, csSup_singleton]

  theorem max013_three : 1 ≤ max013AffineTranslates 3 := by
    apply le_csSup
    · refine ⟨9, ?_⟩
      rintro k ⟨A, hA, rfl⟩
      calc ((A ×ˢ A).filter (fun (x, y) ↦ x ≠ y ∧ x + 3 * (y - x) ∈ A)).card
          ≤ (A ×ˢ A).card := Finset.card_filter_le _ _
        _ = A.card * A.card := Finset.card_product _ _
        _ = 9 := by rw [hA]
    · exact ⟨({0, 1, 3} : Finset ℤ), by decide, by decide⟩

  theorem green_24_no_closed_answer : ¬ ∃ a : ℕ, ∀ n, max013AffineTranslates n = a := by
    rintro ⟨a, ha⟩
    have h0 := ha 0
    have h3 := ha 3
    rw [max013_zero] at h0
    rw [← h0] at h3
    have := max013_three
    omega
  ```

  *Suggested fix.* Green's Problem 24 asks for the growth rate, and the file already records the
  conjecture as `variants.conjecture : gamma = 1/3`. Either make the answer a function,
  `= (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℕ) n` — the idiom used correctly in `OpenQuantumProblems/13.lean`,
  `IsMaxMUBCount d ((answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℕ) d)` — or drop the pointwise headline in favour of
  the asymptotic statement.

- [ ] **`green_16`** — https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/GreensOpenProblems/16.lean#L43-L49

  ```lean
  theorem green_16 (N : ℕ) :
      ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Icc 1 N ∧ SolutionFree A ∧
        A.card = answer(sorry) ∧
        MaximalFor (fun B => B ⊆ Icc 1 N ∧ SolutionFree B) Finset.card A := by sorry
  ```

  `N` is a theorem binder, so a closed answer asserts that the maximum solution-free
  cardinality is the same for every `N`. At `N = 0`, `Icc 1 0 = ∅` forces `A = ∅` and the answer
  to be `0`; at `N = 1`, `{1}` is solution-free (four *distinct* elements are needed to violate
  `SolutionFree`, and `{1}` has one), so `MaximalFor` rules out `∅`.

  ```lean
  theorem green_16_no_closed_answer : ¬ ∃ a : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ,
      ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧ SolutionFree A ∧
        A.card = a ∧
        MaximalFor (fun B => B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧ SolutionFree B) Finset.card A := by
    rintro ⟨a, ha⟩
    obtain ⟨A0, hA0sub, -, hA0card, -⟩ := ha 0
    have hA0 : A0 = ∅ := Finset.subset_empty.mp (by simpa using hA0sub)
    have ha0 : a = 0 := by rw [← hA0card, hA0]; simp
    obtain ⟨A1, -, -, hA1card, hA1max⟩ := ha 1
    have hsub : ({1} : Finset ℕ) ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 1 := by decide
    have hsf : SolutionFree ({1} : Finset ℕ) := by
      intro x hx y hy z hz w hw hnd
      simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at hx hy hz hw
      subst hx; subst hy; subst hz; subst hw
      simp at hnd
    have hle : A1.card ≤ ({1} : Finset ℕ).card := by rw [hA1card, ha0]; simp
    have := hA1max.2 ⟨hsub, hsf⟩ hle
    rw [hA1card, ha0] at this
    simp at this
  ```

  *Suggested fix.* `A.card = (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℕ) N`, i.e. answer with the function `f` the
  file already defines two lines above.

- [ ] **`green_37`** — https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/GreensOpenProblems/37.lean#L46-L50

  ```lean
  theorem green_37 (N k : ℕ) :
      IsLeast { m | ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A.card = m ∧ IsAPCover (A : Set ℕ) N k } (answer(sorry)) := by
    sorry
  ```

  `N` and `k` are binders and the slot has type `ℕ`. At `k = 0` a `0`-term AP is `∅`
  (`Set.IsAPOfLengthWith.zero`), so `∅` is a cover and the least element is `0`; at `k = 2` the
  empty set is not a cover, so `0` is not even a member.

  ```lean
  theorem apCover_zero (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : IsAPCover A N 0 := by
    intro d _
    exact ⟨0, ∅, Set.empty_subset _, by simp⟩

  theorem zero_mem (N : ℕ) :
      (0 : ℕ) ∈ { m | ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A.card = m ∧ IsAPCover (A : Set ℕ) N 0 } :=
    ⟨∅, rfl, by simpa using apCover_zero _ N⟩

  theorem empty_not_cover (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) : ¬ IsAPCover (∅ : Set ℕ) N 2 := by
    intro h
    obtain ⟨a, s, hs, hcard, -⟩ := h 1 ⟨le_refl 1, hN⟩
    rw [Set.subset_empty_iff] at hs
    subst hs
    simp at hcard

  theorem green_37_no_closed_answer :
      ¬ ∃ a : ℕ, ∀ N k : ℕ,
        IsLeast { m | ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A.card = m ∧ IsAPCover (A : Set ℕ) N k } a := by
    rintro ⟨a, ha⟩
    have h0 : a = 0 := Nat.le_zero.mp ((ha 1 0).2 (zero_mem 1))
    obtain ⟨A, hAcard, hAcov⟩ := (ha 1 2).1
    rw [h0, Finset.card_eq_zero] at hAcard
    subst hAcard
    exact empty_not_cover 1 le_rfl (by simpa using hAcov)
  ```

  *Suggested fix.* `IsLeast { … } ((answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) N k)`.

- [ ] **`green_37_asymptotic`** — https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/GreensOpenProblems/37.lean#L52-L59

  ```lean
  theorem green_37_asymptotic (k : ℕ) :
      ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (m N k : ℝ) = (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) N := by sorry
  ```

  Same defect one level up: the slot is a function of `N` but not of `k`, so a closed answer
  must describe `m · k` for **every** `k` at once. `m N 0 = 0` for all `N`, while `m N 1 ≠ 0`
  for `N ≥ 1` (a `1`-term AP is a singleton, so a `1`-cover must be non-empty).

  ```lean
  theorem m_zero (N : ℕ) : m N 0 = 0 := Nat.sInf_eq_zero.mpr (Or.inl (zero_mem N))

  theorem empty_not_cover_one (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) : ¬ IsAPCover (∅ : Set ℕ) N 1 := by
    intro h
    obtain ⟨a, s, hs, hap⟩ := h 1 ⟨le_rfl, hN⟩
    rw [Set.subset_empty_iff] at hs
    subst hs
    rw [show ((1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) = 1 from rfl, Set.IsAPOfLengthWith.one] at hap
    exact (Set.singleton_ne_empty a) hap.symm

  theorem one_cover_nonempty (N : ℕ) :
      { m | ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A.card = m ∧ IsAPCover (A : Set ℕ) N 1 }.Nonempty := by
    refine ⟨1, {0}, by simp, fun d _ => ⟨0, {0}, by simp, ?_⟩⟩
    rw [show ((1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) = 1 from rfl, Set.IsAPOfLengthWith.one]

  theorem m_one_ne_zero (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) : m N 1 ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    rcases Nat.sInf_eq_zero.mp h with h0 | hempty
    · obtain ⟨A, hA, hcov⟩ := h0
      rw [Finset.card_eq_zero] at hA
      subst hA
      exact empty_not_cover_one N hN (by simpa using hcov)
    · exact absurd hempty (Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.mp (one_cover_nonempty N))

  theorem green_37_asymptotic_no_closed_answer :
      ¬ ∃ g : ℕ → ℝ, ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (m N k : ℝ) = g N := by
    rintro ⟨g, hg⟩
    obtain ⟨N, ⟨hN0, hN1'⟩, hN1⟩ :=
      (((hg 0).and (hg 1)).and (eventually_ge_atTop 1)).exists
    rw [m_zero N] at hN0
    rw [← hN0] at hN1'
    exact m_one_ne_zero N hN1 (by exact_mod_cast hN1')
  ```

  *Suggested fix.* `(answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) k N`.

  The sibling `green_37_theta` has the same scoping (its reflexive witness
  `fun N ↦ (m N k : ℝ)` mentions `k`), but there I cannot rule out a single closed function
  serving every `k` up to `Θ`, so I make no claim about it. `green_37_bigO` /
  `green_37_littleO` are being handled in #4943.

- [ ] **`green_41`** — https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/GreensOpenProblems/41.lean#L64-L71

  ```lean
  theorem green_41 :
      ∃ C : ℝ, C > 0 ∧ ∃ ε₀ > 0, ∀ ε ∈ Ioc 0 ε₀,
        let ans := (answer(sorry) : ℝ)
        (minCopies ε : ℝ) ≤ ans ∧ ans < Real.exp (Real.exp (Real.exp (ε ^ (-C)))) := by sorry
  ```

  `ans` is a single real under `∀ ε ∈ Ioc 0 ε₀`, so with a closed answer the statement says
  `minCopies` is **bounded** on `(0, ε₀]` — which is the opposite of what Green asks (how the
  number of rotations grows as `ε → 0`), and false: `pyjamaSet ε` has planar density `2ε`, so a
  union of `n` rotated copies has upper density at most `2εn` and cannot be all of `ℂ` unless
  `n ≥ 1/(2ε)`. Hence `minCopies ε ≥ ⌈1/(2ε)⌉ → ∞`. *(This one I argue rather than machine-check
  — the density bound is standard but I did not formalise it.)*

  *Suggested fix.* The correct form is already eight lines below, in
  `green_41.variants.exists_better_bound`, which puts `∃ ans : ℝ` **inside** the `∀ ε`. Either
  make the answer a function of `ε`, or fold the headline into that variant.

---

# Part B — `green_35`

- [ ] **`green_35.lower` and `green_35.upper` have inert answer slots** —
  https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/GreensOpenProblems/35.lean#L53-L66

  ```lean
  theorem green_35.lower :
      let lb : ℝ≥0∞ → ℝ≥0∞ := answer(sorry)
      (∀ p, 1 < p → lb p ≤ c p) ∧
        (ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (4 / 7)) < c 2 ∨ 0.64 < c ∞) := by sorry
  ```

  The second conjunct — the entire mathematical content — does not mention `lb`, and the first
  is unconditionally true at `lb := 0` because the codomain is `ℝ≥0∞`. So the declaration is
  *equivalent to the bare disjunction*, independently of what is put in the slot. This is not
  the "trivial but uninteresting answer" case: the slot carries no information under **any**
  answer.

  ```lean
  theorem g35_lower_first_conjunct (c : ℝ≥0∞ → ℝ≥0∞) :
      ∀ p : ℝ≥0∞, 1 < p → (0 : ℝ≥0∞ → ℝ≥0∞) p ≤ c p := fun p _ => by simp
  ```

  `green_35.upper` is one step weaker but the same shape: `ub` is pinned only at `⊤`, so the
  declaration is equivalent to `c ∞ < 0.7505`.

  ```lean
  theorem g35_upper_shape (c : ℝ≥0∞ → ℝ≥0∞) (h : c ⊤ < 0.7505) :
      ∃ ub : ℝ≥0∞ → ℝ≥0∞, (∀ p : ℝ≥0∞, 1 < p → c p ≤ ub p) ∧ ub ⊤ < 0.7505 :=
    ⟨fun p => if p = ⊤ then c ⊤ else ⊤, by
      intro p _
      by_cases hp : p = ⊤ <;> simp [hp], by simp [h]⟩
  ```

- [ ] **`green_35.upper` is answerable from Green's own Update 2025.** Fetched from
  https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf today (HTTP 200, 839,479 bytes,
  MD5 `b82b1358949e0e09db84ca3ba1f5e4bd`), Problem 35's comments read, verbatim:

  > The best-known upper bound is *c*∞ ⩽ 0.75049… and this appears in Matolcsi and Vinuesa
  > [224]. … **Update 2025.** An AI-based approach [313] has slightly improved the upper bound
  > of Matolcsi and Vinuesa to *c*∞ ⩽ **0.75026**.

  Reference [313] is *Google DeepMind, AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and
  algorithmic discovery*. Since `0.75026 < 0.7505`, the declaration's own request — a `ub` with
  `ub ∞ < 0.7505` — is met by the published literature the file already cites. The file's
  `variants.c_inf_upper : c ∞ ≤ 0.7505` also records only the superseded Matolcsi–Vinuesa
  bound. I have not checked whether AlphaEvolve's `0.75026` has been independently verified
  beyond Green's own record of it, so "mark solved" may or may not be the right resolution;
  at minimum `variants` should carry the current bound.

---

## Duplicate check

Full-corpus offline sweep (1747 issues, 3237 PRs with per-PR file lists) matched on
declaration name, spaced problem name ("Green 24" as well as `green_24` — GitHub tokenises
underscores) and changed file path, plus a read of #4896, #4923 and #4927 in full. None of the
seven items above appears in any issue. The only open PRs touching these files are #4943
(`green_37_bigO` / `green_37_littleO`, explicitly leaving `green_37`, `green_37_asymptotic` and
`green_37_theta` alone), #4549 (links a formal proof for `green_27.variants.upper_be23`) and
#4004 (docstring LaTeX).

## Relationship to the C₅[K₄] campaign

Found while auditing `research open` declarations in the non-Wikipedia collections. Triage of
all 131 targets, per-item derivations and the duplicate search:

https://github.com/Kuberwastaken/c5-k4/blob/aa598efc894f2ab9628ccd8019b41318f20111ac/results/expansion/live-search-2026-08-15/other-corpora-scan.md

## AI assistance disclosure

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic) for the audit, the Lean witnesses and drafting.
The submitter reviewed each declaration, each proof, and each suggested repair, and takes
responsibility for the submission.

### Choose either option
- [x] I plan on working on this issue
- [ ] This issue is up for grabs: I would like to see this misformalization fixed by somebody else
