Marking `erdos_142.variants.upper` as `research solved` solely with the identity answer `N` may risk suggesting mathematical progress beyond what this proof establishes.

### Additional context
The contribution guide already notes that filling `answer()` and proving the resulting theorem does not by itself constitute a mathematical solution when a trivial or tautological answer is used.

### Describe the misformalization
This report concerns the following `research open` declaration for Erdős Problem 688, part (i), in
`FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/688.lean`:

```lean
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_688.parts.i.upper_bound :
    epsilonFunction =O[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry
```

Source permalink:
https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/d16e05aded22b8c467a0a27c14b2311f53185006/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/688.lean#L45-L51

Because `answer(sorry)` may be an arbitrary comparison function, the declaration only asks for some Big-O upper bound. The constant function `fun _ : ℕ ↦ (1 : ℝ)` already works.

Thus the current Lean declaration can literally be completed without estimating the decay or sharp order of `epsilonFunction`. In particular, this does not prove `epsilonFunction = o(1)` and does not solve Erdős Problem 688.

### Trivial proof/disproof
For `n ≥ 2`, let `ε` satisfy `Erdos688Prop n ε`. Applying the definition at `m = 1` gives a prime `p` such that

```text
n^ε < p ≤ n = n^1.
```

Since `n > 1`, this implies `ε < 1`. If the feasible set is nonempty, exponent `0` is also feasible because every prime is greater than `1`. If it is empty, Lean's totalized supremum is `sSup ∅ = 0`. Therefore

```text
0 ≤ epsilonFunction n ≤ 1
```

for every `n ≥ 2`, and hence

```lean
epsilonFunction =O[atTop] (fun _ : ℕ ↦ (1 : ℝ))
```

### Describe the misformalization
`FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/319.lean` contains the variant `Erdos319.erdos_319.variants.isBigO`.

There is a gap between its docstring and its Lean statement.
The docstring asks for the simplest `g(N)` such that `c = O(g)`, while the Lean statement checks only that one supplied function is an upper bound.
It does not encode that the answer is the simplest or optimal upper bound.


### Trivial proof/disproof
Taking `g(N) = N` works immediately: every admissible set satisfies `A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N`, hence `A.card ≤ N`. The signed unit-fraction condition is not used.

PR: https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/4890

Kernel-checked proof: https://github.com/KitaKen1/erdos-319-linear-upper-bound/blob/3e2cb405aa7c5e2adedcce2c804d704b62c7998a/lean/Erdos319LinearUpperBound.lean#L13-L31

### Suggested fix
Require a matching lower bound or another explicit optimality condition, or reclassify the variant so that an arbitrary upper bound is not treated as a solution.

### Additional context

The same formulation concern was raised during review of PR #4890.

### Describe the misformalization
This concerns Erdős Problem 80 in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/80.lean`.

The two `research open` declarations, `erdos_80` and `erdos_80.variants.log`, quantify over every `c > 0`. This makes both statements false at `c = 2` for an unintended reason.

Permalink: [`80.lean`, lines 51–83](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/8adf5b7d199d83d7c69d2f89d0e7327362ead98a/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/80.lean#L51-L83)

### Trivial proof/disproof
`Admissible c G` means that `G` has at least `cn²` edges and every edge lies in a triangle. The value `f c n` is the minimum, over all such `n`-vertex graphs, of the largest number of triangles sharing one edge. It is `0` if there are no such graphs.

A simple graph on `n` vertices has at most `n(n - 1) / 2` edges. For `c = 2`, at least `2n²` edges would be required, which is impossible for `n ≥ 1`. Hence `f 2 n = 0`. Therefore both open declarations have the answer `False`.

### Suggested fix
Restrict `c` to the feasible range in both declarations, for example `0 < c ∧ c < 1/2`.

### Additional context
The file was introduced in #4830. Original problem: https://www.erdosproblems.com/80

### Describe the misformalization
In the [`FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/SquarePacking.lean`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/c252a41054125b5fd9c8356e2137cd9b55337657/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/SquarePacking.lean#L60-L61), it defines `Circle (r : ℝ)` using only `r ^ 2`. This allows negative radii. As a result, the following two declarations, both currently marked `research open`, can be resolved immediately by disproving their formal statements:

- [`least_three_square_packing_in_circle`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/c252a41054125b5fd9c8356e2137cd9b55337657/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/SquarePacking.lean#L136-L139)
- [`least_fifteen_circle_packing_in_circle`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/c252a41054125b5fd9c8356e2137cd9b55337657/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/SquarePacking.lean#L179-L182)

This does not solve either intended packing problem. The immediate resolution is possible only because the formal statements are misformalized.

### Trivial proof/disproof
- If `0 < r`, then `Circle (-r) = Circle r`, so the same packing is feasible at `-r`, with `-r < r`.
- If `r ≤ 0`, then `r ^ 2 < (r - 1) ^ 2`, hence `Circle r ⊆ Circle (r - 1)`. The same packing is therefore feasible at `r - 1`, with `r - 1 < r`.

Thus every feasible radius has a smaller feasible radius, so no least element exists.

### Suggested fix
Restrict the candidate radii to nonnegative reals:

```lean
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem least_three_square_packing_in_circle :
    IsLeast
      {r : ℝ | 0 ≤ r ∧ Nonempty (Packing 3 UnitSquare (Circle r))}
      answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem least_fifteen_circle_packing_in_circle :
    IsLeast
      {r : ℝ | 0 ≤ r ∧ Nonempty (Packing 15 UnitCircle (Circle r))}
      answer(sorry) := by
  sorry
```

Alternatively, use `ℝ≥0` for the radius type.

### Additional context
This affects 2 of the 5 declarations marked `research open`. The other 3 minimize `Square x` and are unaffected.

### Describe the misformalization

[`BoundedBurnsideProblem.lean`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/e923379e609b9d5987011a1d1f06ec22ea25cd20/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/BoundedBurnsideProblem.lean#L26-L36) formalizes the universal claim that every finitely generated group of bounded exponent is finite, but leaves its answer unknown and tags it `research open`:

```lean
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem bounded_burnside_problem :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (fin_gen : Group.FG G)
      (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 0) (bounded : ∀ g : G, g^n = 1), Finite G := by
  sorry
```

The [cited Burnside-problem source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnside_problem#Bounded_Burnside_problem) records infinite finitely generated groups of bounded exponent, including counterexamples for every sufficiently large odd exponent. The exact universal proposition in Lean therefore has a known negative answer.

### Trivial proof/disproof

An infinite finitely generated group of exponent $n$ satisfies every hypothesis on the right-hand side but is not `Finite G`. Such counterexamples are the classical negative solution to the bounded-exponent question.

### Suggested fix

Replace `answer(sorry)` with `answer(False)`, change the category to `research solved`, and update the theorem docstring to state and reference the known negative answer. Keep the group-theoretic predicate unchanged.

### Additional context

The broader classification problem asking for which ranks and exponents the free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is finite remains open. This correction only records the known answer to the universal yes/no proposition currently formalized.

- [ ] This issue is up for grabs: I would like to see this misformalization fixed by somebody else

OpenAI Codex was used to compare the cited source with the Lean declaration, identify the status/answer mismatch, and prepare the proposed correction.

body:
### Describe the misformalization

[`erdos_562`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/71d34fc2958f1010ee43ccd4d54a9631574d7ef9/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/562.lean#L38-L41) relates `log^[r-1] (R_r(n))` and `n` by **`~[atTop]`** (`Asymptotics.IsEquivalent`), but the informal statement asks for **`≍_r`** (Hardy's `\asymp`, i.e. same order of magnitude, `Θ`, with `r`-dependent implied constants). `~` is **strictly stronger** than `≍`, so the formal statement over-constrains the problem.

```lean
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_562 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ r ≥ 3, (fun n ↦ log^[r - 1] (hypergraphRamsey r n)) ~[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry
```

In Mathlib `f ~[l] g` (`Asymptotics.IsEquivalent`) is `(f - g) =o[l] g`, i.e. `f / g → 1` — strictly stronger than `f =Θ[l] g`. So `~[atTop]` demands the iterated logarithm be asymptotically *equal* to `n` with leading constant exactly `1`; the intended `≍` only asks it be of the same *order*. A solver proving the intended `Θ`-bound would not satisfy the formalized `~`, and the formal statement may be false as written (no reason the constant is `1`).

### Trivial proof/disproof

`~ ⟹ Θ` is a Mathlib lemma (`Asymptotics.IsEquivalent.isTheta`), `sorry`-free:

```lean
example (f g : ℕ → ℝ) (h : f ~[atTop] g) : f =Θ[atTop] g := h.isTheta
```

The converse fails — `(fun n ↦ 2 * n) =Θ[atTop] (fun n ↦ n)` but **not** `(fun n ↦ 2 * n) ~[atTop] (fun n ↦ n)` (ratio → `2`, not `1`). So `~` is *strictly* stronger than `≍`/`=Θ`: the current statement is a different (stronger, likely false) claim than the one Erdős poses.

### Suggested fix

Replace `~[atTop]` with `=Θ[atTop]` (`Asymptotics.IsTheta`), which is exactly `≍` (`=Θ[·]` is already in scope via `open scoped Asymptotics`):

```lean
    ∀ r ≥ 3, (fun n ↦ log^[r - 1] (hypergraphRamsey r n)) =Θ[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ))
```

### Additional context

Related to — but distinct from — the open discussion in #33 (*`answer(sorry)` and asymptotic problems*): that asks whether an `answer(sorry)` captures *optimality*; this is the *relation* (`≍` vs `~`). Surfaced by an automated formal-vs-informal fidelity screen, then confirmed by reading the docstring's `\asymp` against the Mathlib meaning of `~[atTop]` plus the lemma above.

The fix is the single-token change above. Flagging it as **up for grabs** — happy for a maintainer or contributor to apply it; I may follow up with the PR once I'm set up to run the full FC build.
title: Erdős Problem 562 — misformalisation: `~[atTop]` (asymptotic equivalence) used where the statement says `≍` (same order / Θ)

body:
# Erdős Problem 274 — misformalisation: `(Set.range P.parts).Pairwise` is vacuously true under constant parts

The current formalization of [`erdos_274`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/274.lean#L57-L59) admits a **trivial witness** that does not match the mathematical intent of the Erdős problem (existence of an exact covering by cosets of *distinct sizes*).

## The current formalization

```lean
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem erdos_274 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (G : Type*) (h : Group G) (hG : 1 < ENat.card G)
    (ι : Type*) (_ : Fintype ι) (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι),
      1 < Fintype.card ι ∧ (Set.range P.parts).Pairwise fun A B ↦ #A ≠ #B := by
  sorry
```

## The bug

The condition `(Set.range P.parts).Pairwise fun A B ↦ #A ≠ #B` is **vacuously true** when `P.parts` is constant (all cosets use the same subgroup). `Set.range P.parts` deduplicates and is a singleton in that case; `Pairwise` quantifies only over *distinct* elements, so there are no pairs to check.

## Trivial witness reproducing the bug

Take `G = ZMod 2` (the cyclic group of order 2), `ι = Fin 2`, and:
- `P.parts = fun _ => ⊥` (both cosets use the trivial subgroup)
- `P.reps = ![0, 1]` (distinct representatives)

The cosets `0 • ⊥ = {0}` and `1 • ⊥ = {1}` partition `ZMod 2`. The conditions hold:
- `1 < ENat.card (ZMod 2)` ✓ (card = 2)
- `1 < Fintype.card (Fin 2)` ✓ (card = 2)
- `(Set.range P.parts).Pairwise fun A B ↦ #A ≠ #B` ✓ — **vacuously**, because `Set.range P.parts = {⊥}` is a singleton

Yet mathematically the two cosets have **equal size** (both = 1 element). This is *not* a counterexample to the spirit of the Erdős/Herzog–Schönheim question, which asks for cosets of **distinct sizes**.

The Lean file's *other* theorems already use the correct quantifier pattern:

```lean
theorem erdos_274.variants.abelian ... :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j) := by sorry  -- correct: per-index

theorem herzog_schonheim ... :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ (P.parts i).index = (P.parts j).index := by sorry  -- correct: per-index
```

Only `erdos_274` itself uses the buggy `Set.range`-based formulation.

## Proposed fix

Change the condition in `erdos_274` from
```lean
(Set.range P.parts).Pairwise fun A B ↦ #A ≠ #B
```
to
```lean
∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) ≠ #(P.parts j)
```

This aligns the main theorem with the existing `variants.abelian` and `herzog_schonheim` formulations in the same file, and matches the original Erdős/Herzog–Schönheim mathematical statement.

## Analogy with issue #1137 (erdos_707)

This is a different bug pattern than #1137 (which involved allowing `n = 0` in a Sidon-set context) but belongs to the same class : *a small Lean quantifier choice produces a statement that is logically valid but does not match the natural-language intent*. Same fix pattern: tighten the quantification so the witness must do work.

## How this was found

Detected on 2026-05-26 by a Gemini 3.1 Pro Deep Think one-shot batch evaluation of the [Hubble erdos-unsolved](https://github.com/) sprint top-30 candidates. Gemini flagged the disconnect between the Lean statement and the mathematical intent ; the bug was confirmed by manual reading of the theorem's quantifier structure.

Happy to provide a PR with the one-line fix if useful.
title: Erdős Problem 274 — misformalisation: `Set.range P.parts` makes the existential trivially satisfiable

body:
### Describe the misformalization
The ERH statement at https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/60d13721bee9c49a21ee6510e2cf924637e47725/FormalConjectures/Millenium/RiemannHypothesis.lean#L127 can prove `False` with the following example. The problem is that Mathlib's `NumberField.dedekindZeta` has not been extended to the entire complex plane, thus producing junk zeros.

### Trivial proof/disproof
```lean
import Mathlib

--- The following is taken from FormalConjectures/Millenum/RiemannHypothesis.Lean
def IsInCriticalStrip (s : ℂ) : Prop :=
  0 < s.re ∧ s.re < 1


def trivialZeros (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] : Set ℤ :=
  by
    classical
    exact if NumberField.IsTotallyReal K then { -2 * n | (n : ℕ) } else Set.Iic 0

theorem extended_riemann_hypothesis_dedekindZeta (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] (s : ℂ)
    (hs : NumberField.dedekindZeta K s = 0)
    (hs_nontrivial : s ∉ Int.cast '' trivialZeros K)
    (hs_ne_one : s ≠ 1) :
    s.re = 1 / 2 := by
  sorry
--- end of FormalConjectures/Millenum/RiemannHypothesis.Lean snippet

noncomputable def idealEquiv : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ℚ) ≃o Ideal ℤ := RingEquiv.idealComapOrderIso Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.symm

noncomputable def idealSubtypeEquiv (b : ℕ) : { I : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ℚ) // Ideal.absNorm I = b } ≃ { I : Ideal ℤ // Ideal.absNorm I = b } := by
  refine idealEquiv.subtypeEquiv ?_
  intro a
  congrm ?_ = _
  simp only [Ideal.absNorm_apply, Submodule.cardQuot, idealEquiv, RelIso.coe_fn_toEquiv,
    RingEquiv.idealComapOrderIso_apply, Ideal.comap_symm]
  have : RingHomSurjective Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.toRingHom := ⟨Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.surjective⟩
  rw [show Ideal.map Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv a = Submodule.map Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.toRingHom.toSemilinearMap a from Ideal.map_eq_submodule_map Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.toRingHom _]
  rw [show (Submodule.map Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.toRingHom.toSemilinearMap a).toAddSubgroup = a.toAddSubgroup.map Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.toAddEquiv from rfl]
  symm
  apply AddSubgroup.index_map_equiv (Submodule.toAddSubgroup a)

theorem card_ideal (b : ℕ) : Nat.card { I : Ideal ℤ // Ideal.absNorm I = b } = 1 := by
  rw [Nat.card_eq_one_iff_exists]
  refine ⟨⟨Ideal.span {(b : ℤ)}, by simp⟩, ?_⟩
  intro ⟨y, hy⟩
  simp [← hy]

theorem dedekind_quarter : NumberField.dedekindZeta ℚ (1 / 4 : ℂ) = 0 := by
  simp_rw [NumberField.dedekindZeta, LSeries, LSeries.term]
  apply tsum_eq_zero_of_not_summable
  simp_rw [fun b ↦ Nat.card_congr (idealSubtypeEquiv b), card_ideal]
  suffices ¬Summable fun (b : ℕ) => (1 / ↑b ^ (1 / 4 : ℂ) : ℂ) by
    convert this using 3 with b
    split_ifs with h
    · simp [h]
    simp
  rw [Complex.summable_one_div_nat_cpow]
  norm_num

theorem false : False := by
  have h := extended_riemann_hypothesis_dedekindZeta ℚ (1 / 4) dedekind_quarter (by 
    simp only [one_div, Set.mem_image, not_exists, not_and]
    intro x _ h
    obtain h := congr(4 * $h)
    simp at h
    norm_cast at h
    grind)
  simp at h

```

### Suggested fix
A proper definition that extends `NumberField.dedekindZeta` to the entire complex plane needs to be introduced first.

- [x] This issue is up for grabs: I would like to see this misformalization fixed by somebody else

### Describe the misformalization
`Erdos522.erdos_522` appears to formalize a weaker **in-probability** statement, rather than the **almost-sure** statement given in the informal problem description.

Permalink:
https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/522.lean

More specifically:

- The informal statement on erdosproblems.com/522 is:
  “If `R_n` is the number of roots of `f(z)` in `{z ∈ ℂ : |z| ≤ 1}`, then `R_n / (n/2) → 1` almost surely.”
- The docstring for `Erdos522.erdos_522` repeats that informal statement.
- But the theorem statement itself is of the form
  `P(|R_n - n/2| ≥ o(n) * n) ≤ p(n)` with `p(n) → 0`,
  which is an in-probability style claim.
- The same file already contains `Erdos522.erdos_522.variants.yakir_solution` as a solved variant, and that theorem is also of in-probability type.

So the current main theorem seems to encode the weaker Yakir-type formulation rather than the almost-sure Erdős problem.

### Trivial proof/disproof
I do not have a trivial Lean proof/disproof here.

This seems to be a **faithfulness mismatch** rather than a theorem that is obviously false in Lean: the current formal statement may well be mathematically true, but it does not appear to match the intended informal statement. So I do not currently have a short counterexample showing the formal theorem is false; the issue is that it is weaker than the problem text it is supposed to represent.

### Suggested fix
One of these seems appropriate:

1. **Change `erdos_522` to an actual almost-sure formulation**, if the intent is to formalize the Erdős problem as stated on erdosproblems.com.

2. If an almost-sure encoding is not yet convenient, **rename/reword `erdos_522`** so that it is explicitly presented as an in-probability proxy / weakened formalization, rather than as the Erdős problem itself.

3. Keep `erdos_522.variants.yakir_solution` as the solved in-probability result, and make the distinction between:
   - the open almost-sure problem, and
   - the solved in-probability variant
   completely explicit in the main theorem’s docstring and statement.

### Additional context
Relevant sources:

- erdosproblems.com/522 states the problem with **almost surely**
- the discussion thread explicitly says Yakir solved a **weaker** version “in probability”
- the current `522.lean` docstring for `erdos_522` uses the informal almost-sure wording, but its “Formalization note” and theorem statement are in-probability in nature
- the same file already includes `yakir_solution` as a separate solved result

I’d be happy to work on this, including the Lean-side formalization/update, though I’d probably appreciate an extra pair of eyes to sanity-check the intended almost-sure formulation against the current in-probability one.

If a maintainer or someone else would prefer to take it, I’m also happy to leave it to them.

- [x] I plan on working on this issue
- [ ] This issue is up for grabs: I would like to see this misformalization fixed by somebody else

### Describe the misformalization
The statement for [Erdos Problem 331](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/331.lean) should be 'for all sets A and B, if A and B have a certain growth rate, then infinitely many differences exist'. However, I believe that it currently reads 'for all sets A and B, A and B have a certain growth rate and infinitely many differences exist'. This is trivially false by letting A and B be empty, for example.

https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/6f95d2c23a77f06a221de374cc05fa62973d736e/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/331.lean

### Trivial proof/disproof
theorem erdos_331 :
    (False) ↔
      ∀ A B : Set ℕ,
      (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (count A n : ℝ)) ∧
      (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (count B n : ℝ)) ∧
      { s : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | let ⟨a₁, a₂, b₁, b₂⟩ := s
        a₁ ∈ A ∧ a₂ ∈ A ∧ b₁ ∈ B ∧ b₂ ∈ B ∧
        a₁ ≠ a₂ ∧ a₁ + b₂ = a₂ + b₁ }.Infinite := by
  simp +zetaDelta at *;
  -- Let's choose $A = \emptyset$ and $B = \emptyset$.
  use ∅, ∅; simp

### Suggested fix
My attempted fix, but please verify:

theorem erdos_331 :
    (False) ↔
      ∀ A B : Set ℕ,
      ((fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (count A n : ℝ)) ∧
      (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (count B n : ℝ))) →

### Describe the misformalization
Erdős problem 480 is still misformalized.

This was previously reported in https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/issues/1282 but then closed in https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/1540

### Trivial proof/disproof
Here is an example proof:
```
theorem erdos_480 : ∀ (x : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ n, x n ∈ Set.Icc 0 1) →
    ⨅ n, atTop.liminf (fun m => n * |x (m + n) - x m|) ≤ 1 / √5 := by
  field_simp;
  intro x hx;
  refine' le_trans ( mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ( ciInf_le _ 0 ) ( Real.sqrt_nonneg _ ) ) _ <;> norm_num [ Filter.liminf_const ];
  refine' ⟨ 0, Set.forall_mem_range.2 fun n => _ ⟩;
  refine' le_csSup _ _ <;> norm_num;
  · exact ⟨ n * 1, by rintro a ⟨ m, hm ⟩ ; exact le_trans ( hm m le_rfl ) ( mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ( show |x ( m + n ) - x m| ≤ 1 by exact abs_le.mpr ⟨ by linarith [ Set.mem_Icc.mp ( hx ( m + n ) ), Set.mem_Icc.mp ( hx m ) ], by linarith [ Set.mem_Icc.mp ( hx ( m + n ) ), Set.mem_Icc.mp ( hx m ) ] ⟩ ) ( Nat.cast_nonneg _ ) ) ⟩;
  · exact ⟨ 0, fun _ _ => mul_nonneg ( Nat.cast_nonneg _ ) ( abs_nonneg _ ) ⟩
```

The variant `erdos_480.variants.chung_graham` is also easily provable.

### Suggested fix
The `inf` is for `n=0`.  There was a problem before wherein the code divided by $n$, so that was a hint that one should have the condition $n\ne 0$.  Now the formulation doesn't divide by $n$ anymore, but $n=0$ should still be avoided.

EDIT TO ADD: I missed that the formalization requires `k > 0`, unlike in the paper. The statement in the paper seemed to be missing an epsilon dependence, but maybe it was actually missing a positivity constraint on k. The statement in the repo is at least not totally trivial, then, but I still think the paper meant to have an epsilon dependence of some sort.

### Describe the misformalization
The statement [here](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/c1249b6a157bb39e5120cfe09ef084ae643d4d74/FormalConjectures/Arxiv/1506.05785/MaximumAngle.lean#L41) is mistaken. In fact, the conjecture written in https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.05785v4 is wrong - they made a typo and it's trivial as a result.

I believe the authors meant `〈a, b/5^k 〉 \ge 1 − \epsilon * 5^(−k / (2−δ)`. Currently there's no epsilon dependence.

### Trivial proof/disproof
A trivial solution: pick `k=0`. Then the RHS of the inequality become `1 - 1 = 0`, so the only requirement is that a doesn't have a negative inner product with b/5^k. This can be accomplished by taking any axis (any basis vector), and then the unit vector in either the positive or negative direction will have positive inner product.

### Suggested fix
The quanliy of approximation needs to depend on epsilon. Really any nontrivial dependence will do (since epsilon can be rescaled as needed...) but I think it was meant to be a product as I wrote.

```
  -- Let's choose any $x \in \ell^\infty$.
  intro x hx;
  refine Set.infinite_of_injective_forall_mem ( fun m n hmn => by aesop ) fun m => ⟨ m + 1, 0, ?_, ?_, rfl ⟩ <;> norm_num
```

### Suggested fix
Change m ≠ 0 to n ≠ 0.

### Additional context
There was a little bit of interaction here with the "garbage" value 1/0 = 0 in Mathlib, which could have helped spot the error.

### Choose either option
- [ ] I plan on working on this issue
- [x] This issue is up for grabs: I would like to see this misformalization fixed by somebody else
title: Erdős problem 480 trivial proof
Erdős problem 56 bounds issue

body:
### Describe the misformalization
Erdős problem 707 asks whether a finite Sidon set can always be extended to a (finite!) perfect difference set.  https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/707

The file https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/707.lean has several versions of this conjecture, one of which is called `erdos_707.variants.weaker`:
https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/707.lean#L65-L71

There is a minor oversight here, in that the natural number `n` might be zero.  This is not the intended conjecture.

### Trivial proof/disproof
It is not hard to see that every Sidon set can be extended to a perfect difference set in Z/nZ with n=0.  (The proof is "just do it".)

For what it's worth, I have tried proving this in Lean and found it difficult...

### Suggested fix
Add the condition that n is nonzero.

### Additional context
The conjecture has been resolved, as reported in the forums [here](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/707#post-1350).  It is false.  This includes `erdos_707` and `erdos_707.variants.weaker`.

A counterexample is {1,2,4,8,13}.  A Lean proof IS available.

As a result, the inclusion/exclusion of `n=0` flips the truth value of `erdos_707.variants.weaker`.
title: Erdős Problem 707 minor issue
